```svelte
    {
      id: "c",
      name: "Load Balancer 2",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",
    },
    {
      id: "d",
      name: "Load Balancer 6",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "e",
      name: "Load Balancer 4",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 443,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "f",
      name: "Load Balancer 5",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",
    },
  ]}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="expandIcon" let:expanded let:props>
    <Add
      {...props}
      style="display: inline-block; transition: transform 0.2s ease; transform: {expanded
        ? 'rotate(45deg)'
        : 'rotate(0deg)'}"
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="expandedRow" let:row>
    <pre>{JSON.stringify(row, null, 2)}</pre>
  </svelte:fragment>
</DataTable>
```

```svelte
<script>

      protocol: "HTTP",

      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",
    },

      name: "Load Balancer 6",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 3000,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "e",
      name: "Load Balancer 4",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 443,
      rule: "Round robin",
    },
    {
      id: "f",
      name: "Load Balancer 5",
      protocol: "HTTP",
      port: 80,
      rule: "DNS delegation",

  ];

  batchExpansion
```

#### With selection

Combine `batchExpansion` and `batchSelection` for expandable, selectable tables.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let expandedRowIds = [];
  let selectedRowIds = [];

  $: {
    console.log("expandedRowIds", expandedRowIds);
    console.log("selectedRowIds", selectedRowIds);
  }
</script>

<DataTable
  batchExpansion
  batchSelection
  bind:expandedRowIds
  bind:selectedRowIds
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
    { key: "rule", value: "Rule" },
  ]}
  rows={Array.from({ length: 6 }).map((_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    name: `Load Balancer ${i + 1}`,
    protocol: "HTTP",
    port: i % 3 ? (i % 2 ? 3000 : 80) : 443,
    rule: i % 3 ? "Round robin" : "DNS delegation",
  }))}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="expandedRow" let:row>
    <pre>{JSON.stringify(row, null, 2)}</pre>
  </svelte:fragment>
</DataTable>
```

### Events

Listen for clicks and hovers on headers, rows, and cells--for example, to open a detail view when a row is clicked. For the sortable header's cancelable `sort` event, see [Sorting](#sortable-columns).

#### Row and cell clicks

`click:row` fires when a row is clicked and `click:cell` fires for the specific cell, with `event.detail.target`/`currentTarget` identifying what was clicked. `click:header` fires for header cells. A generic `click` event also fires alongside each of these, with whichever of `header`, `row`, or `cell` applies to that click.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTable
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
  ]}
  rows={[
    { id: "a", name: "Load Balancer 3", protocol: "HTTP", port: 3000 },
    { id: "b", name: "Load Balancer 1", protocol: "HTTP", port: 443 },
    { id: "c", name: "Load Balancer 2", protocol: "HTTP", port: 80 },
  ]}
  on:click:row={(e) => console.log("click:row", e.detail.row)}
  on:click:cell={(e) => console.log("click:cell", e.detail.cell)}
  on:click:header={(e) => console.log("click:header", e.detail.header)}
/>
```

#### Row hover

`mouseenter:row` and `mouseleave:row` fire when the pointer enters or leaves a row, with the row data as `event.detail`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTable } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTable
  headers={[
    { key: "name", value: "Name" },
    { key: "protocol", value: "Protocol" },
    { key: "port", value: "Port" },
  ]}
  rows={[
    { id: "a", name: "Load Balancer 3", protocol: "HTTP", port: 3000 },
    { id: "b", name: "Load Balancer 1", protocol: "HTTP", port: 443 },
    { id: "c", name: "Load Balancer 2", protocol: "HTTP", port: 80 },
  ]}
  on:mouseenter:row={(e) => console.log("mouseenter:row", e.detail)}
  on:mouseleave:row={(e) => console.log("mouseleave:row", e.detail)}
/>
```

### Skeleton

Show a loading state with `DataTableSkeleton`.

#### Loading state

Use the data table skeleton to show a loading state.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTableSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTableSkeleton />
```

#### Headers and rows

Specify headers and row count for the skeleton.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTableSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTableSkeleton headers={["Name", "Protocol", "Port", "Rule"]} rows={10} />
```

#### Object headers

Pass header objects to customize the skeleton.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTableSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTableSkeleton
  headers={[
    { value: "Name" },
    { value: "Protocol" },
    { value: "Port" },
    { value: "Rule" },
  ]}
  rows={10}
/>
```

#### Empty header

Add an empty header column with `empty: true`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTableSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTableSkeleton
  headers={[
    { value: "Name" },
    { value: "Protocol" },
    { value: "Port" },
    { value: "Rule" },
    { empty: true },
  ]}
  rows={10}
/>
```

#### No header or toolbar

Hide the header and toolbar in the skeleton.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTableSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTableSkeleton showHeader={false} showToolbar={false} />
```

#### Medium

Set `size="medium"` to explicitly match the default `DataTable` row height.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTableSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTableSkeleton showHeader={false} showToolbar={false} size="medium" />
```

#### Tall

Set `size="tall"` for a taller skeleton.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTableSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTableSkeleton showHeader={false} showToolbar={false} size="tall" />
```

#### Short

Set `size="short"` for a shorter skeleton.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTableSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DataTableSkeleton showHeader={false} showToolbar={false} size="short" />
```

#### Compact

Set `size="compact"` for a minimal skeleton.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DataTableSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";

<DataTableSkeleton showHeader={false} showToolbar={false} size="compact" />
```

### Component API

#### `DataTable` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sortKey` (Reactive) | `DataTableKey<Row>` | Specify the header key to sort by. | `null` |
| `sortDirection` (Reactive) | `"none" \| "ascending" \| "descending"` | Specify the sort direction. | `"none"` |
| `expandable` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` for the expandable variant.<br />Automatically set to `true` if `batchExpansion` is `true`. | `false` |
| `expandedRowIds` (Reactive) | `ReadonlyArray<Row["id"]>` | Specify the row ids to be expanded. | `[]` |
| `selectedRowIds` (Reactive) | `ReadonlyArray<Row["id"]>` | Specify the row ids to be selected. | `[]` |
| `scrollContainerRef` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLDivElement` | Obtain a reference to the table wrapper element. When virtualization is enabled and `stickyHeader` is false, this element is the scroll container--use `bind:scrollContainerRef` to programmatically control scroll position (e.g. `scrollContainerRef.scrollTop = 0`). | `null` |
| `headers` | `ReadonlyArray<DataTableHeader<Row>>` | Specify the data table headers. | `[]` |
| `rows` | `ReadonlyArray<Row>` | Specify the rows the data table should render.<br />Keys defined in `headers` are used for the row ids. | `[]` |
| `size` | `"compact" \| "short" \| "medium" \| "tall"` | Set the size of the data table. | _undefined_ |
| `title` | `string` | Specify the title of the data table | `""` |
| `description` | `string` | Specify the description of the data table | `""` |
| `rowClass` | `DataTableRowClass<Row>` | Specify a custom class name for each row.<br />Provide a function to return a class name based<br />on row properties, allowing conditional classes<br />based on selected/expanded state. | _undefined_ |
| `inputName` | `string` | Specify a name attribute for the input elements<br />in a selectable data table (radio or checkbox).<br />When the table is inside a form, this name will<br />be included in the form data on submit. | `uniqueId()` |
| `zebra` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use zebra styles | `false` |
| `sortable` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for the sortable variant. Individual columns can opt out (or, if this is `false`, opt in) via `header.sort`. | `false` |
| `sortAlways` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to only toggle between "ascending" and<br />"descending" sort directions, skipping "none". | `false` |
| `sort` | `(a: DataTableSortValue<Row>, b: DataTableSortValue<Row>, context: { key: DataTableKey<Row>; ascending: boolean; row_a: Row; row_b: Row }) => number` | Specify a default sort comparator for all sortable columns.<br />Per-header `sort` functions take precedence over this prop.<br /><br />With a typed row generic, `a` and `b` are {@link DataTableSortValue} (the union of cell value types over every {@link DataTableKey} on `Row`). Narrow using `context.key` (typed as {@link DataTableKey}) or runtime checks. | _undefined_ |
| `batchExpansion` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable batch expansion. | `false` |
| `nonExpandableRowIds` | `ReadonlyArray<Row["id"]>` | Specify the ids for rows that should not be expandable. | `[]` |
| `radio` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for the radio selection variant.<br />Row selection is enabled regardless of `selectable`. | `false` |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for the selectable variant.<br />Shift-clicking a row checkbox extends selection to every row between it and the last row clicked (not supported with `radio`). | `false` |
| `batchSelection` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable batch selection.<br />Row selection is enabled regardless of `selectable`. | `false` |
| `nonSelectableRowIds` | `ReadonlyArray<Row["id"]>` | Specify the ids of rows that should not be selectable. | `[]` |
| `highlightedRowIds` | `ReadonlyArray<Row["id"]>` | Specify the row ids to highlight.<br />Adds `bx--data-table--highlighted-row`. The highlighted row class is themed by default. | `[]` |
| `stickyHeader` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable a sticky header | `false` |
| `stickyHeaderMaxHeight` | `number \| string` | Override the maximum height of the sticky header table, replacing the<br />default `300px`. Only applies when `stickyHeader` is `true`. Pass a number<br />(interpreted as `px`) or a CSS length string (e.g. `"100%"`, `"24rem"`). | _undefined_ |
| `useStaticWidth` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use static width | `false` |
| `filterMode` | `"remove" \| "hide"` | Set the filtering strategy used by `ToolbarSearch`.<br />- `"remove"`: remove non-matching rows from the DOM and recreate them when the<br /> filter clears.<br />- `"hide"`: keep all rows mounted and hide non-matching rows with the `hidden`<br /> attribute, preserving focus, inputs, and open menus.<br /><br />`"hide"` falls back to `"remove"` when `pageSize` is set or `virtualize` is enabled.<br /><br />Because `"hide"` keeps every row mounted, each keystroke re-renders all<br />rows, not just matching ones. For large row counts (hundreds or more),<br />prefer `"remove"`, pagination, or virtualization. | `"remove"` |
| `pageSize` | `number` | Specify the number of items to display in a page | `0` |
| `page` | `number` | Set to `number` to set current page | `0` |
| `virtualize` | `undefined \| boolean \| { itemHeight?: number, maxVisibleRows?: number, containerHeight?: number, overscan?: number, threshold?: number, maxItems?: number }` | Enable virtualization for large row lists. Virtualization renders only the rows currently visible in the viewport, improving performance for large datasets.<br /><br />Virtualization is opt-in. Set `virtualize={true}` to enable with default settings, or pass a configuration object to customize.<br />Virtualized tables are intended for use with `stickyHeader={true}` so the header stays visible while scrolling. Pagination is ignored when virtualization is enabled.<br />Virtualization assumes a uniform row height; combining it with `expandable` rows is not supported and may cause incorrect scroll-spacer sizing when rows are expanded mid-list.<br /><br />Provide an object to customize virtualization behavior:<br />- `itemHeight` (default: 48 for medium size, adjusted for size variant): The height in pixels of each row. Specify a custom value when using custom slots with multi-line content or different heights.<br />- `maxVisibleRows` (default: 10): The maximum number of rows to display in the viewport. The container height will be calculated as `itemHeight * maxVisibleRows`. Overridden by `containerHeight` if explicitly provided.<br />- `containerHeight` (default: calculated from maxVisibleRows): The maximum height in pixels of the table body container. If not provided, calculated from `itemHeight * maxVisibleRows`.<br />- `overscan` (default: 3): The number of extra rows to render above and below the viewport for smoother scrolling. Higher values may cause more flickering during very fast scrolling.<br />- `threshold` (default: 100): The minimum number of rows required before virtualization activates. Tables with fewer rows will render all rows normally without virtualization.<br />- `maxItems` (default: undefined): The maximum number of rows to render. When undefined, all visible rows are rendered. | _undefined_ |
| `tableHeaderTranslateWithId` | `(id: import("./TableHeader.svelte").TableHeaderTranslationId) => string` | Override the default table header translation ids. | _undefined_ |
| `refreshRow` | `(id: Row["id"]) => void` | Rebuild cells for a single row after an in-place edit to `rows`. | _undefined_ |
| `refreshCells` | `() => void` | Rebuild cells for currently painted rows after batch in-place edits to<br />`rows`. Offscreen rows are computed when they enter the window. | _undefined_ |

#### `DataTable` typedefs

```ts
type DataTableValue = any;

interface DataTableRow<Id = any> {
  id: Id;
  [key: string]: DataTableValue;
}

type DataTableKey<Row = DataTableRow> = [
  keyof import("./data-table-utils.d.ts").KeysWithoutIndexSignature<Row>,
] extends [never]
  ? import("./data-table-utils.d.ts").PropertyPath<Row>
  : keyof import("./data-table-utils.d.ts").KeysWithoutIndexSignature<Row> extends "id"
    ? import("./data-table-utils.d.ts").PropertyPath<Row>
    : Row extends DataTableRow
      ? import("./data-table-utils.d.ts").PropertyPathIgnoringIndexSignatures<Row>
      : import("./data-table-utils.d.ts").PropertyPath<Row>;

type DataTableSortValue<Row = DataTableRow> =
  import("./data-table-utils.d.ts").DataTableSortValue<Row>;

type DataTableEmptyHeader<Row = DataTableRow> = {
  key: DataTableKey<Row> | (string & {});
  /** Whether the header is empty */
  empty: true;
  display?: (item: DataTableValue, row: Row) => DataTableValue;
  /** `false` disables sorting for this column even when the table is sortable; `true` enables it even when the table is not; a comparator both enables sorting and provides it. Unset inherits the table-level `sortable`. */
  sort?:
    | boolean
    | ((a: DataTableSortValue<Row>, b: DataTableSortValue<Row>) => number);
  /** Override table-level sortAlways for this column */
  sortAlways?: boolean;
  /** Whether the column menu is enabled */
  columnMenu?: boolean;
  /** Whether the column is skipped in render while remaining in `headers` */
  columnHidden?: boolean;
  width?: string;
  minWidth?: string;
};

type DataTableNonEmptyHeader<Row = DataTableRow> = {
  key: DataTableKey<Row>;
  empty?: false;
  value: DataTableValue;
  display?: (item: DataTableValue, row: Row) => DataTableValue;
  /** `false` disables sorting for this column even when the table is sortable; `true` enables it even when the table is not; a comparator both enables sorting and provides it. Unset inherits the table-level `sortable`. */
  sort?:
    | boolean
    | ((a: DataTableSortValue<Row>, b: DataTableSortValue<Row>) => number);
  /** Override table-level sortAlways for this column */
  sortAlways?: boolean;
  /** Whether the column menu is enabled */
  columnMenu?: boolean;
  /** Whether the column is skipped in render while remaining in `headers` */
  columnHidden?: boolean;
  width?: string;
  minWidth?: string;
  /** Horizontal alignment of the column header and cells. Logical, so `end` is the right edge in LTR and the left edge in RTL. Defaults to `"start"`. */
  columnAlign?: "start" | "end";
};

type DataTableHeader<Row = DataTableRow> =
  DataTableNonEmptyHeader<Row> | DataTableEmptyHeader<Row>;

type DataTableCell<Row = DataTableRow> = {
  key: DataTableKey<Row> | (string & {});
  value: DataTableValue;
  display?: (item: DataTableValue, row: DataTableRow) => DataTableValue;
};

interface DataTableRowClassArgs<Row = DataTableRow> {
  row: Row;
  rowIndex: number;
  selected: boolean;
  expanded: boolean;
}

type DataTableRowClass<Row = DataTableRow> =
  string | ((row: DataTableRowClassArgs<Row>) => string | undefined);
```

## DatePicker

### Calendar types

DatePicker supports five `datePickerType` values: `"simple"` (default, no calendar), `"single"`, `"range"`, `"month"`, and `"year"`.

#### Simple

The default `datePickerType` renders a text field without a dropdown calendar.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Date of birth" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Single

Set `datePickerType` to `"single"` for one date with a dropdown calendar. Use a single DatePickerInput; clicking the field or calendar icon opens the calendar to pick one day. Bind `value` to read or set the formatted date string.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Range

Set `datePickerType` to `"range"` for a start and end date. Provide two DatePickerInput components in order--start, then end--and bind `valueFrom` and `valueTo`. Both fields share one calendar: the user selects a span, and the start and end inputs update together.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="range" on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Start date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  <DatePickerInput labelText="End date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

##### Programmatic

Use `bind:valueFrom` and `bind:valueTo` to update the range from outside the component, such as preset buttons or filters.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let valueFrom = "01/01/2024";
  let valueTo = "01/31/2024";

  function advanceMonth(value) {
    var d = new Date(value);
    var month = d.getMonth() + 1;
    var year = d.getFullYear() + (month > 11 ? 1 : 0);
    month = month % 12;
    var lastDay = new Date(year, month + 1, 0).getDate();
    var day = Math.min(d.getDate(), lastDay);
    var mm = String(month + 1).padStart(2, "0");
    var dd = String(day).padStart(2, "0");
    return `${mm}/${dd}/${year}`;
  }

  function nextMonth() {
    valueFrom = advanceMonth(valueFrom);
    valueTo = advanceMonth(valueTo);
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <DatePicker datePickerType="range" bind:valueFrom bind:valueTo on:change>
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Start date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
    <DatePickerInput labelText="End date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <Button on:click={nextMonth}>Next month</Button>
</Stack>
```

#### Month

Set `datePickerType` to `"month"` to select a month instead of a day. The calendar shows a 12-month grid for the current year; use the year stepper to change years. Pair it with a `dateFormat` that omits the day, such as `"F Y"` (for example, "January 2026").

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="month" dateFormat="F Y" on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Billing month" placeholder="Month Year" />
</DatePicker>
```

##### Custom format

Pass a numeric `dateFormat`, such as `"Y-m"`, along with a matching `placeholder` for a compact "yyyy-mm" input.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="month" dateFormat="Y-m" on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Billing month" placeholder="yyyy-mm" />
</DatePicker>
```

##### Programmatic

Use `bind:value` to update the selected month from outside the component, such as a "previous month" button.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "03/2026";

  function previousMonth() {
    var [month, year] = value.split("/").map(Number);
    var d = new Date(year, month - 2, 1);
    var mm = String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, "0");
    value = `${mm}/${d.getFullYear()}`;
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <DatePicker datePickerType="month" dateFormat="m/Y" bind:value on:change>
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Billing month" placeholder="mm/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <Button on:click={previousMonth}>Previous month</Button>
</Stack>
```

#### Year

Set `datePickerType` to `"year"` to select a year instead of a day. The calendar shows a decade grid; use the prev/next controls to move between decades. Pair it with a year-only `dateFormat` such as `"Y"` (for example, "2026").

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="year" dateFormat="Y" on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Fiscal year" placeholder="yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

##### Programmatic

Use `bind:value` to select a year from outside the component, or `bind:calendar` to move the displayed decade--such as jumping to the current year or paging forward--without changing the selection.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
  let calendar = null;

  function selectCurrentYear() {
    value = String(new Date().getFullYear());
  }

  function viewNextDecade() {
    calendar?.changeYear(calendar.currentYear + 10);
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <DatePicker
    datePickerType="year"
    dateFormat="Y"
    bind:value
    bind:calendar
    on:change
  >
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Fiscal year" placeholder="yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <Stack gap={3} orientation="horizontal">
    <Button kind="tertiary" on:click={selectCurrentYear}>
      Select current year
    </Button>
    <Button kind="tertiary" on:click={viewNextDecade}>View next decade</Button>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

### Calendar options

Configure constraints and behavior shared by single, range, month, and year calendars.

#### Min and max dates

Use `minDate` and `maxDate` to constrain selectable dates. Values may be a Date, or a string in the same format as `dateFormat`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const start = new Date(2025, 0, 1);
  const end = new Date(2025, 11, 31);
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" minDate={start} maxDate={end} on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Date (2025 only)" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Flatpickr options

Use `flatpickrProps` to pass additional [Flatpickr options](https://flatpickr.js.org/options/). These merge with the options Carbon sets internally (for example static positioning, clickOpens, and top-layer appendTo when using `portalMenu`). Override props such as static only when you understand how they interact with portalling and modals.

The example below sets `showMonths` so two months appear side by side in the calendar.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker
  datePickerType="single"
  flatpickrProps={{ showMonths: 2 }}
  on:change
>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Calendar-only selection

By default, Carbon enables Flatpickr allowInput so typed dates work like an editable field.

Pass `flatpickrProps={{ allowInput: false }}` when you want calendar-only selection: the field still receives the chosen date and remains focusable for accessibility, but users cannot free-type into the input--they must pick a date from the calendar. That reduces invalid or ambiguous typed values when you need strict control.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker
  datePickerType="single"
  flatpickrProps={{ allowInput: false }}
  on:change
>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Ship date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Disable open animation

By default, the calendar animates when it opens and closes. Pass `flatpickrProps={{ animate: false }}` to disable the [Flatpickr animate option](https://flatpickr.js.org/options/) and show the calendar instantly.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" flatpickrProps={{ animate: false }}>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Date of birth" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Keep open on select

By default, the calendar closes when a date is selected. Pass `closeOnSelect: false` via `flatpickrProps` to keep it open.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" flatpickrProps={{ closeOnSelect: false }}>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Programmatic access

Use `bind:calendar` to access the underlying [Flatpickr instance](https://flatpickr.js.org/instance-methods-properties-elements/) for programmatic control, such as opening the calendar from an external trigger or updating options at runtime via `set`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let calendar = null;
  let weekendsDisabled = false;

  function openCalendar(e) {
    // Prevent the click from bubbling to the outside click
    // handler and closing the calendar immediately.
    e.stopPropagation();
    calendar?.open();
  }

  function toggleWeekends() {
    weekendsDisabled = !weekendsDisabled;
    calendar?.set(
      "disable",
      weekendsDisabled
        ? [(date) => date.getDay() === 0 || date.getDay() === 6]
        : [],
    );
  }
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <DatePicker datePickerType="single" bind:calendar on:change>
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Appointment" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <Stack gap={3} orientation="horizontal">
    <Button kind="tertiary" on:click={openCalendar}>Open calendar</Button>
    <Button kind="tertiary" on:click={toggleWeekends}>
      {weekendsDisabled ? "Enable" : "Disable"}
      weekends
    </Button>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

### Formatting

Customize the date format and locale.

#### Date format

Use the `dateFormat` prop to customize the date format (default: `"m/d/Y"`). The input pattern attribute is automatically derived to match, ensuring native form validation works correctly.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
  let submittedValue = "";
</script>

<form on:submit|preventDefault={() => (submittedValue = value)}>
  <Stack inline gap={4}>
    <DatePicker bind:value datePickerType="single" dateFormat="Y-m-d">
      <DatePickerInput
        labelText="Date of birth"
        placeholder="yyyy-mm-dd"
        helperText={submittedValue ? `Submitted: ${submittedValue}` : ""}
      />
    </DatePicker>
    <Button type="submit" disabled={!value}>Submit</Button>
  </Stack>
</form>
```

#### Locale

The `locale` prop accepts either a [flatpickr locale key](https://github.com/flatpickr/flatpickr/tree/master/src/l10n) or a [CustomLocale](https://github.com/flatpickr/flatpickr/blob/master/src/types/locale.ts) object. It defaults to `"en"`, which renders Carbon-spec single-letter weekday abbreviations (S, M, T, W, Th, F, S).

To customize the weekday labels (for example, to restore flatpickr's default English `Sun, Mon, Tue, ...` shorthands), pass a `CustomLocale` object.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const englishLongShorthand = {
    weekdays: {
      shorthand: ["Sun", "Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat"],
      longhand: [
        "Sunday",
        "Monday",
        "Tuesday",
        "Wednesday",
        "Thursday",
        "Friday",
        "Saturday",
      ],
    },
  };
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" locale={englishLongShorthand} on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Non-English locale

Import the corresponding locale module from `flatpickr/dist/l10n/<key>` and pass it to the `locale` prop. The example below uses German (`de`).

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import { German } from "flatpickr/dist/l10n/de";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" locale={German} on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Termin" placeholder="tt.mm.jjjj" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Locale with year-first order

For locales where `Intl.DateTimeFormat` orders the year before the month (for example Japanese), the calendar header automatically reorders to match--"2000年1月" instead of "January 2000".

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import { Japanese } from "flatpickr/dist/l10n/ja";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" locale={Japanese} on:change>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="日付" placeholder="yyyy/mm/dd" />
</DatePicker>
```

### Portal

Set `portalMenu` to `true` to render the calendar in a floating portal. This prevents the calendar from being clipped by parent containers with `overflow: hidden` or z-index stacking contexts. Inside a [Modal](/components/Modal), `portalMenu` defaults to `true` unless explicitly set to `false`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Modal,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Select date</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  size="sm"
  modalHeading="Meeting date"
  primaryButtonText="Confirm"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
>
  <DatePicker datePickerType="single">
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
</Modal>
```

#### Native dialog

When the date picker is inside a [Dialog](/components/Dialog) opened as a modal, portalMenu mounts the calendar into that dialog so it appears above the modal backdrop. The calendar uses `position: fixed` with viewport coordinates.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    Dialog,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Open dialog</Button>

<Dialog bind:open modal aria-label="Meeting scheduler">
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <p>
      With <code>portalMenu</code>, the calendar auto-mounts into the nearest
      <code>&lt;dialog&gt;</code>
      ancestor so it renders above the modal backdrop.
    </p>
    <DatePicker portalMenu datePickerType="single">
      <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
    </DatePicker>
    <Button kind="secondary" on:click={() => (open = false)}>Close</Button>
  </Stack>
</Dialog>
```

#### Native popover

When the date picker is inside an open element with a [popover](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/popover) attribute (see the [Popover API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API)), portalMenu mounts the calendar into that ancestor so it stays in the popover top layer.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let popover = null;
</script>

<Button type="button" on:click={() => popover?.showPopover()}
  >Open popover</Button
>

<div
  bind:this={popover}
  popover="manual"
  style="width: min(100%, 28rem); padding: 1rem; border: 1px dashed var(--cds-border-subtle);"
>
  <p>
    With <code>portalMenu</code>, the calendar auto-mounts into the nearest
    <code>[popover]</code>
    ancestor so it renders in the popover top layer instead of behind it.
  </p>
  <DatePicker portalMenu datePickerType="single">
    <DatePickerInput labelText="Meeting date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  </DatePicker>
  <Button
    kind="secondary"
    type="button"
    on:click={() => popover?.hidePopover()}
  >
    Close
  </Button>
</div>
```

### Events

Listen for calendar interactions.

#### Change

Listen for `on:change` to respond to value updates. For the `"simple"` date picker type (no calendar), `event.detail` is the input's string value. For calendar types (`"single"`, `"range"`, `"month"`, `"year"`), `event.detail` is an object with `selectedDates` (an array of `Date`) and `dateStr` (a string, or `{ from, to }` for `"range"`).

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" on:change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Date of birth" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Close

Listen for `on:close` to know when the calendar closes and why. This event is only dispatched for calendar types (not `"simple"`). `event.detail.trigger` is `"escape-key"`, `"outside-click"`, or `"select"`; the detail also includes `selectedDates` and `dateStr`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker
  datePickerType="single"
  on:close={(e) => console.log(e.detail.trigger)}
>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Date of birth" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

### Helper text

Add helper text to provide additional context or formatting instructions.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker>
  <DatePickerInput
    labelText="Date of birth"
    helperText="Example: 01/12/1990"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker>
  <DatePickerInput
    hideLabel
    labelText="Date of birth"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

### Light

Use the light variant for light backgrounds.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker light>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Date of birth" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

### Fluid

Set `fluid` to `true` on DatePicker to use the fluid variant, which embeds the label inside the field. Fluid date pickers can be used standalone or inside [FluidForm](/components/FluidForm), where the fluid variant is applied automatically.

Standalone fluid date pickers default to `288px` wide so the field matches the calendar menu. Inside a fluid form they stretch to `100%` of the column. Override the width with `style` or `class` when you need a different size (for example `style="width: 50%"`).

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="single">
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Date of birth" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Simple

The fluid variant also supports the default `"simple"` date picker type.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid>
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Date of birth" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Range

The range date picker renders both inputs inside a single fluid field.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="range">
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Start date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  <DatePickerInput labelText="End date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Month

The fluid variant also supports the `"month"` date picker type.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="month" dateFormat="F Y">
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Billing month" placeholder="Month Year" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Year

The fluid variant also supports the `"year"` date picker type.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="year" dateFormat="Y">
  <DatePickerInput labelText="Fiscal year" placeholder="yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    DatePicker,
    DatePickerInput,
    TooltipIcon,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="single">
  <DatePickerInput placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy">
    <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
      Date of birth
      <TooltipIcon
        tooltipText="Use the format mm/dd/yyyy."
        icon={Information}
      />
    </svelte:fragment>
  </DatePickerInput>
</DatePicker>
```

#### Invalid

Fluid date pickers display the error message inside the field boundary. Long messages wrap to multiple lines.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="single">
  <DatePickerInput
    invalid
    invalidText="The provided date is not valid. Enter a date in the mm/dd/yyyy format that falls within the allowed range."
    labelText="Date of birth"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Warning

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="single">
  <DatePickerInput
    warn
    warnText="This date will not be stored"
    labelText="Date of birth"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Disabled

Invalid and warning states are not displayed while the input is disabled.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="single" value="01/15/1990">
  <DatePickerInput
    disabled
    invalid
    invalidText="The provided date is not valid"
    labelText="Date of birth"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Read-only

Invalid and warning states are not displayed while the input is read-only.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker fluid datePickerType="single" value="01/15/1990">
  <DatePickerInput
    readonly
    warn
    warnText="This date will not be stored"
    labelText="Date of birth"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

Display a loading skeleton for the fluid date picker variant. Set `range` to `true` to mimic the range variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { FluidDatePickerSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<FluidDatePickerSkeleton />
```

```svelte

<FluidDatePickerSkeleton range />
```

### States

Reflect validation and interaction states.

#### Invalid

Show an invalid state when the input value is not valid.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker>
  <DatePickerInput
    invalid
    invalidText="Invalid date"
    labelText="Date of birth"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Warning

Show a warning state to indicate potential issues with the input.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker>
  <DatePickerInput
    warn
    warnText="This info will not be stored"
    labelText="Date of birth"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Disabled (simple)

With the default datePickerType (`"simple"`), disabled prevents interaction and styles the field as unavailable.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker value="01/15/1990">
  <DatePickerInput
    disabled
    labelText="Date of birth"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Disabled (single)

Set `disabled` to `true` to block interaction with the single-date picker and calendar.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" value="01/15/1990">
  <DatePickerInput
    disabled
    labelText="Date of birth"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Disabled (range)

Apply disabled to each DatePickerInput in a range picker when both fields should be unavailable.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="range" valueFrom="01/01/2025" valueTo="01/31/2025">
  <DatePickerInput disabled labelText="Start date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  <DatePickerInput disabled labelText="End date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Read-only (simple)

With the default datePickerType (`"simple"`), readonly shows a fixed value in the text field without a calendar.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker value="01/15/1990">
  <DatePickerInput
    readonly
    labelText="Date of birth"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Read-only (single)

Set `readonly` to `true` to display a value while preventing edits. Unlike disabled, the input remains focusable and its value is submitted with the form.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="single" value="01/15/1990">
  <DatePickerInput
    readonly
    labelText="Date of birth"
    placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

#### Read-only (range)

The readonly state also works with range pickers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DatePicker datePickerType="range" valueFrom="01/01/2025" valueTo="01/31/2025">
  <DatePickerInput readonly labelText="Start date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  <DatePickerInput readonly labelText="End date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

### Component API

#### `DatePicker` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `number \| string` | Specify the date picker input value. | `""` |
| `valueFrom` (Reactive) | `string` | Specify the date picker start date value (from).<br />Only works with the "range" date picker type. | `""` |
| `valueTo` (Reactive) | `string` | Specify the date picker end date value (to).<br />Only works with the "range" date picker type. | `""` |
| `calendar` (Reactive) | `import("flatpickr/dist/types/instance").Instance \| null` | Bind to the Flatpickr calendar instance for programmatic control.<br />Only available when `datePickerType` is `"single"`, `"range"`, `"month"`,<br />or `"year"`.<br />@see https://flatpickr.js.org/instance-methods-properties-elements/ | `null` |
| `datePickerType` | `"simple" \| "single" \| "range" \| "month" \| "year"` | Specify the date picker type. | `"simple"` |
| `dateFormat` | `string` | Specify the date format.<br />Use `"F Y"` or `"m/Y"` with `datePickerType="month"`, and `"Y"` with<br />`datePickerType="year"`. | `"m/d/Y"` |
| `maxDate` | `null \| string \| Date` | Specify the maximum date. | `null` |
| `minDate` | `null \| string \| Date` | Specify the minimum date. | `null` |
| `locale` | `import("flatpickr/dist/types/locale").CustomLocale \| import("flatpickr/dist/types/locale").key` | Specify the locale. | `"en"` |
| `short` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the short variant | `false` |
| `light` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable the light variant | `false` |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the fluid variant.<br />Inherited from the parent `FluidForm` context,<br />so it does not need to be set when used inside `FluidForm`. | `false` |
| `portalMenu` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set to `true` to render the calendar in a portal to prevent clipping.<br />When inside a Modal, defaults to `true` unless explicitly set to `false`.<br /><br />When the date picker is inside a native `<dialog>` (opened with<br />`showModal()`) or an open `[popover]` element, the calendar auto-mounts<br />into that top-layer ancestor and uses `position: fixed` so it renders<br />above the backdrop instead of behind it. | _undefined_ |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the date picker element | `uniqueId()` |
| `flatpickrProps` | `import("flatpickr/dist/types/options").Options` | Override the options passed to the Flatpickr instance.<br />@see https://flatpickr.js.org/options | `{ static: true }` |

#### `DatePicker` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `DatePicker` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `DatePicker` dispatched events

| Event | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `on:change` | `type EventDetail =<br />  \| string<br />  \| {<br />      selectedDates: [<br />        dateFrom: Date,<br />        dateTo?: Date,<br />      ];<br />      dateStr:<br />        \| string<br />        \| { from: string; to: string };<br />    }` |
| `on:close` | `{<br />  trigger:<br />    \| "escape-key"<br />    \| "outside-click"<br />    \| "select";<br />}` |

#### `DatePicker` $$restProps

`DatePicker` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.

#### `DatePickerInput` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLInputElement` | Obtain a reference to the input HTML element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "xl"` | Set the size of the input. | _undefined_ |
| `type` | `string` | Specify the input type | `"text"` |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Specify the input placeholder text | `""` |
| `pattern` | `string` | Specify the Regular Expression for the input value.<br />By default, the pattern is derived from the parent<br />`DatePicker`'s `dateFormat` prop. | _undefined_ |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the input | `false` |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to mark the input as read-only | `false` |
| `helperText` | `string` | Specify the helper text | `""` |
| `iconDescription` | `string` | Specify the ARIA label for the calendar icon | `""` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the input element | `uniqueId()` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text | `false` |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate an invalid state | `false` |
| `invalidText` | `string` | Specify the invalid state text | `""` |
| `warn` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate a warning state | `false` |
| `warnText` | `string` | Specify the warning state text | `""` |
| `name` | `string` | Set a name for the input element. | _undefined_ |

#### `DatePickerInput` slots

| Slot            | Detail                  |
| --------------- | ----------------------- |
| `labelChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `DatePickerInput` forwarded events

| Event        |
| ------------ |
| `on:blur`    |
| `on:focus`   |
| `on:input`   |
| `on:keydown` |
| `on:keyup`   |
| `on:paste`   |

#### `DatePickerInput` $$restProps

`DatePickerInput` spreads `$$restProps` to the `input` element.

#### `DatePickerSkeleton` props

| Prop    | Type      | Description                            | Default |
| ------- | --------- | -------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `range` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the range variant | `false` |
| `short` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the short variant | `false` |

#### `DatePickerSkeleton` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `DatePickerSkeleton` $$restProps

`DatePickerSkeleton` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.

#### `FluidDatePickerSkeleton` props

| Prop    | Type      | Description                            | Default |
| ------- | --------- | -------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `range` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the range variant | `false` |

#### `FluidDatePickerSkeleton` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `FluidDatePickerSkeleton` $$restProps

`FluidDatePickerSkeleton` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## Dialog

### Basic

Open the dialog by binding to `open`. `Dialog` opens non-modally by default, using the browser's `show()`: it renders without a backdrop, and the rest of the page stays interactive. `Dialog` has no built-in heading, so provide an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` attribute; both forward to the underlying dialog element.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Dialog, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Open dialog</Button>

<Dialog bind:open aria-label="Example dialog">
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <p>This dialog has no backdrop. The page behind it stays interactive.</p>
    <Button on:click={() => (open = false)}>Close</Button>
  </Stack>
</Dialog>
```

### Modal

Set `modal` to `true` to open the dialog with the browser's `showModal()`, which adds a backdrop and confines focus and interaction to the dialog.

`Dialog` renders only what you put in its default slot, with no built-in header, footer, or action buttons. Use it to build a custom overlay, or as the top-layer host for portalled content such as DatePicker or FloatingPortal. For a ready-made dialog with a heading, body, and action buttons, use [Modal](/components/Modal) instead.

When the dialog opens, focus moves into it (native modal focus trap). When it closes, focus returns to the element that opened it.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Dialog, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Open modal dialog</Button>

<Dialog
  bind:open
  modal
  aria-label="Example modal dialog"
  on:open={() => console.log("open")}
  on:close={(e) => console.log("close", e.detail)}
>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <p>Dialog content.</p>
    <form method="dialog">
      <Button type="submit">Close</Button>
    </form>
  </Stack>
</Dialog>
```

### Events

`Dialog` dispatches `open` once the dialog becomes visible (after `show()`/`showModal()` runs and focus moves in). Pair it with `close` -- see [Closing](#closing) below -- to track the dialog's full lifecycle.

```svelte
<Dialog
  bind:open
  on:open={() => console.log("open")}
  on:close={(e) => console.log("close", e.detail)}
>
```

### Closing

The `close` event includes a `trigger` property indicating what dismissed the dialog: `"escape-key"` (<kbd>Escape</kbd>), `"backdrop"`, `"close-button"` (for example a `<form method="dialog">` submit), or `"programmatic"` (when `open` is set to `false`).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Dialog, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
  let lastTrigger = null;
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Open modal dialog</Button>
  {#if lastTrigger}
    <p>Last close trigger: <code>{lastTrigger}</code></p>
  {/if}
</Stack>

<Dialog
  bind:open
  modal
  aria-label="Close trigger example"
  on:close={(e) => {
    lastTrigger = e.detail.trigger;
    console.log("close", e.detail);
  }}
>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <p>
      Dismiss with <kbd>Escape</kbd>, the backdrop, the close button, or by
      setting <code>open</code> to <code>false</code>.
    </p>
    <form method="dialog">
      <Button type="submit">Close</Button>
    </form>
  </Stack>
</Dialog>
```

#### Prevent on outside click

Disable closing the modal dialog when clicking the backdrop with `preventCloseOnClickOutside`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Dialog, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Open dialog</Button>

<Dialog
  preventCloseOnClickOutside
  bind:open
  modal
  aria-label="Prevent outside click example"
>
  <Stack gap={5}>
    <p>
      Clicking the backdrop will not close this dialog. Use
      <kbd>Escape</kbd>
      or the close button.
    </p>
    <form method="dialog">
      <Button type="submit">Close</Button>
    </form>
  </Stack>
</Dialog>
```

---

### Component API

#### `Dialog` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the dialog. | `false` |
| `modal` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render the dialog as a modal using `showModal()`.<br />When `false`, the dialog opens non-modally using `show()`.<br />Changing `modal` while `open` is `true` has no effect until the dialog closes and reopens. | `false` |
| `preventCloseOnClickOutside` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to prevent the dialog from closing when clicking the backdrop.<br />Only applies when `modal` is `true`. | `false` |

#### `Dialog` typedefs

```ts
type DialogCloseTrigger =
  "escape-key" | "backdrop" | "close-button" | "programmatic";
```

#### `Dialog` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `Dialog` forwarded events

| Event      |
| ---------- |
| `on:click` |

#### `Dialog` dispatched events

| Event      | Detail                                         |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `on:close` | `{<br />  trigger: DialogCloseTrigger;<br />}` |
| `on:open`  | `null`                                         |

#### `Dialog` $$restProps

`Dialog` spreads `$$restProps` to the `dialog` element.


## Disclosure

### Basic

Create a disclosure with `summary` for the always-visible trigger text and a default slot for the content it shows or hides.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Disclosure } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Disclosure summary="Show shipping details">
  <p>Orders ship within 2 business days and arrive in 3-5 business days.</p>
</Disclosure>
```

### Left-aligned chevron

Align the chevron icon to the left side of the trigger by setting `align` to `"start"`. The default is `"end"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Disclosure } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Disclosure align="start" summary="Show shipping details">
  <p>Orders ship within 2 business days and arrive in 3-5 business days.</p>
</Disclosure>
```

### Custom summary slot

Customize the trigger content with the summary slot instead of `summary` for more complex layouts with multiple elements.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Disclosure } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Disclosure>
  <svelte:fragment slot="summary">
    <strong>Shipping details</strong>
    <span>Ships in 2 days</span>
  </svelte:fragment>
  <p>Orders ship within 2 business days and arrive in 3-5 business days.</p>
</Disclosure>
```

### Open state

Control whether the disclosure starts open, and read or drive its state programmatically.

#### Open by default

Set `open` to `true` to render the disclosure expanded.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Disclosure } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Disclosure open summary="Show shipping details">
  <p>Orders ship within 2 business days and arrive in 3-5 business days.</p>
</Disclosure>
```

#### Reactive (two-way binding)

Bind to `open` to control and read the disclosure state outside the component. Listen for `toggle` to react to state changes, such as when the trigger is activated with a click or the keyboard.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Disclosure, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <div>Open: <strong>{open}</strong></div>
  <Disclosure
    bind:open
    summary="Show shipping details"
    on:toggle={(e) => console.log("toggle", e.detail)}
  >
    <p>Orders ship within 2 business days and arrive in 3-5 business days.</p>
  </Disclosure>
</Stack>
```

---

### Component API

#### `Disclosure` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the disclosure. | `false` |
| `summary` | `string` | Specify the summary content of the trigger.<br />Alternatively, use the "summary" slot. | `""` |
| `align` | `"start" \| "end"` | Specify alignment of the chevron icon. | `"end"` |

#### `Disclosure` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |
| `summary` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `Disclosure` forwarded events

| Event             |
| ----------------- |
| `on:animationend` |
| `on:blur`         |
| `on:click`        |
| `on:focus`        |
| `on:keydown`      |
| `on:mouseenter`   |
| `on:mouseleave`   |
| `on:mouseover`    |

#### `Disclosure` dispatched events

| Event       | Detail    | Description                         |
| ----------- | --------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `on:toggle` | `boolean` | Dispatched with the new open state. |

#### `Disclosure` $$restProps

`Disclosure` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## Dropdown

### Basic

Use the dropdown to create a select input with a dropdown menu. Each item needs a unique id.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  labelText="Contact"
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Selection

Control which item is selected through `selectedId`.

#### No selection

Omit `selectedId` to render the dropdown with no item selected. The label appears as placeholder text until the user makes a selection.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Choose a contact method"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Clearable

Set `clearable` to `true` to show a clear button when an item is selected. Clearing resets `selectedId` and dispatches a `clear` event. The clear button is hidden when there is no selection.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  clearable
  labelText="Contact"
  selectedId="0"
  label="Choose a contact method"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Clear button text

Override the assistive text for the clear interaction with `clearSelectionText` (appended to the field's description whenever there is a selection to clear) and `selectionClearedText` (announced through the status live region after clearing). Both only apply when `clearable` is `true`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  clearable
  clearSelectionText="Press Escape twice to clear"
  selectionClearedText="Contact method cleared"
  labelText="Contact"
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Initial selection

Set `selectedId` to pre-select an item when the dropdown first renders. The trigger shows that item's label in the closed state.

When the user opens the menu, if the option list is taller than the menu's maximum height, the menu scrolls so the selected option stays visible. That applies to lists rendered in full and to [virtualized lists](#large-lists).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 50 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Item ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedId = 42;
</script>

<Dropdown labelText="Items" {items} bind:selectedId />
```

### Content

Customize the label, item display, and supporting text.

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot for custom label content instead of `labelText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
>
  <strong slot="labelChildren">Custom label</strong>
</Dropdown>
```

#### Custom slot

Override the default slot to customize the display of each item. Use `let:item`, `let:index`, `let:selected`, and `let:highlighted` to style highlighted and selected rows.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  labelText="Contact"
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  let:item
  let:index
  let:selected
  let:highlighted
>
  <div>
    <strong>{item.text}</strong>
  </div>
  <div>
    id: {item.id} - index: {index} - selected: {selected} - highlighted:
    {highlighted}
  </div>
</Dropdown>

<style>
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item),
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item__option) {
    height: auto;
  }
</style>
```

#### Item icons

Set icon on an item for a left icon. The label sits between the icon and the checkmark. Use the icon slot for custom markup.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  labelText="Contact"
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack", icon: Chat },
    { id: "1", text: "Email", icon: Email },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax", icon: Document },
  ]}
/>
```

Use the `iconRight` slot to replace the checkmark.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Star from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Star.svelte";
  import StarFilled from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/StarFilled.svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  labelText="Contact"
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack", icon: Chat },
    { id: "1", text: "Email", icon: Email },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax", icon: Document },
  ]}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="icon" let:item>
    <svelte:component this={item.icon} />
  </svelte:fragment>
  <svelte:fragment slot="iconRight" let:selected>
    {#if selected}<StarFilled />{:else}<Star />{/if}
  </svelte:fragment>
</Dropdown>
```

#### Format display text

Format item display text with `itemToString`. The function receives each item and returns the formatted string.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  itemToString={(item) => {
    return item.text + " (" + item.id + ")";
  }}
  labelText="Contact"
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>

### Helper text Add descriptive text below the dropdown with `helperText`.

<Dropdown
  helperText="Choose your preferred contact method"
  labelText="Contact"
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>

### Hidden label Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The
label remains available to screen readers.

<Dropdown
  hideLabel
  labelText="Contact"
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>

## Menu Control the menu's position, portalling, and open state. ### Top
direction Set `direction` to `"top"` to open the menu above the input. Useful
when space below is limited.

<Dropdown
  direction="top"
  labelText="Contact"
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>

### Portal menu Set `portalMenu` to `true` to render the dropdown menu in a
floating portal. This prevents the menu from being clipped by parent containers
with `overflow: hidden` or z-index stacking contexts. Without `portalMenu`, the
dropdown in the example below would be clipped by its container's hidden
overflow. When inside a [Modal](/components/Modal#modal-with-dropdowns),
`portalMenu` defaults to `true` unless explicitly set to `false`.
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack
  gap={4}
  style="overflow: hidden; border: 1px dashed var(--cds-border-subtle); padding: 1rem; max-height: 120px;"
>
  <div>
    This container has hidden overflow. Without <code>portalMenu</code>, the
    dropdown would be clipped.
  </div>
  <Dropdown
    portalMenu
    labelText="Preferred channel"
    selectedId="0"
    items={[
      { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
      { id: "1", text: "Email" },
      { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
    ]}
  />
</Stack>
```

#### Open by default

Set `open` to `true` to render the dropdown already expanded. The prop is bindable (`bind:open`), so you can also drive it externally, such as from a trigger elsewhere on the page.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  open
  labelText="Contact"
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Wrapped options

Option labels are truncated to one line. At a 320px viewport, that hides text and can leave two options looking identical, a WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow failure.

Set `wrapOptions` to let a label take as many lines as it needs. Lines break between words, and mid-word only when a word is too long to fit a line by itself. A [custom slot](#custom-slot) wraps with the label.

It defaults to `false` because wrapping changes option heights.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const roles = [
    "Chief Accessibility Officer for Regional Operations and Strategic Partnerships",
    "Deputy Director of Interdepartmental Communications and Outreach",
  ];

  const items = [
    { id: "0", text: roles[0] },
    { id: "1", text: roles[1] },
    { id: "2", text: "Analyst" },
  ];

  // Past the count at which a list is windowed, so only the options on screen
  // are rendered. `wrapOptions` turns on measured row heights by itself, so
  // offsets follow the heights the wrapped options actually take.
  const manyItems = Array.from({ length: 300 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: String(i),
    text: `${i + 1}. ${roles[i % 2]}`,
  }));
</script>

<Stack gap={6} style="max-width: 20rem;">
  <Dropdown labelText="Truncated (default)" selectedId="2" {items} />
  <Dropdown wrapOptions labelText="Wrapped" selectedId="2" {items} />
  <Dropdown
    wrapOptions
    labelText="Wrapped (windowed, 300 items)"
    items={manyItems}
  />
</Stack>
```

### Virtualization

Virtualization renders only the items currently visible in the viewport, improving performance for large lists.

#### Large lists

By default, the dropdown virtualizes lists with more than 100 items.

In the example below, 10,000 items are provided to the dropdown but only 11 items (8 visible items + 3 overscan items) are rendered in the DOM.

Set `virtualize={false}` to explicitly disable virtualization, even for large lists. Or customize the threshold at which virtualization activates. See [Custom threshold](#custom-threshold).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Item ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedId = 1000;
  $: selectedItem = items.find((item) => item.id === selectedId);
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <Dropdown
    labelText="Virtualized Dropdown (10,000 items)"
    {items}
    bind:selectedId
  />
  <div>
    <strong>Selected:</strong>
    {selectedItem?.text}
  </div>
</Stack>
```

#### Load more

`scrollend` fires when the menu is scrolled near the bottom so you can append the next page of `items`. Same pattern as [ComboBox load more](/components/ComboBox#load-more): handle `on:scrollend`, keep prior items visible while loading, and track in-flight status locally (or with the `empty` slot when appropriate). The event is a near-bottom load-more signal, not the browser's native `scrollend`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown {items} on:scrollend={() => loadNextPage()} />
```

#### Custom overscan

Overscanning is the process of rendering extra items above and below the viewport to ensure smooth scrolling. The default overscan value is 3.

Specify a custom value for `overscan` to control how many extra items render above and below the viewport for smoother scrolling.

During very fast scrolling, higher overscan values may cause more flickering due to increased DOM updates. For fast-scrolling scenarios, use a lower overscan value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Item ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedId = 1000;
</script>

<Dropdown
  virtualize={{ overscan: 100 }}
  labelText="High overscan (10,000 items, overscan: 100)"
  {items}
  bind:selectedId
/>
```

#### Custom threshold

The threshold is the minimum number of items required before virtualization activates. The default threshold value is 100, meaning lists with fewer than 100 items will not be virtualized and all items will be rendered normally.

Specify a custom value for `threshold` to control when virtualization activates. Below the threshold, all items render normally without virtualization.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 100 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Item ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedId = 50;
</script>

<Dropdown
  virtualize={{ threshold: 200 }}
  labelText="Custom threshold (threshold: 200)"
  {items}
  bind:selectedId
/>
```

#### Custom item height

By default, item height matches the menu row for each size: 24px (`xs`), 32px (`sm`), 40px (`md`), 48px (`lg`, `xl`). Set `itemHeight` when custom slots change row height.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Item ${i + 1}`,
    description: `Description for item ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedId = 1000;
</script>

<Dropdown
  virtualize={{ itemHeight: 60 }}
  labelText="Custom item height (60px)"
  {items}
  bind:selectedId
  let:item
>
  <Stack gap={2}>
    <strong>{item.text}</strong>
    <span>{item.description}</span>
  </Stack>
</Dropdown>

<style>
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item),
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item__option) {
    height: auto;
  }
</style>
```

#### Custom container height

The virtualized menu's scrollable container defaults to a maximum height of 300px. Set `containerHeight` within the `virtualize` object to change it. Providing any `virtualize` object (even with a short list, as below) activates the sizing behavior, though items only get windowed once the list reaches `threshold`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  virtualize={{ containerHeight: 150 }}
  labelText="Contact"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
    { id: "3", text: "Phone" },
    { id: "4", text: "Mail" },
    { id: "5", text: "SMS" },
    { id: "6", text: "WhatsApp" },
    { id: "7", text: "Teams" },
    { id: "8", text: "Zoom" },
    { id: "9", text: "In person" },
  ]}
/>
```

Set `maxItems` within the same object to cap the number of items rendered in the DOM window at once, independent of `overscan`. This only takes effect once the list is windowed (at or above `threshold`), and is rarely needed outside of extreme item counts or very expensive item templates--set it too low and items can appear to go blank near the scroll edges.

### Multiple dropdowns

Create multiple dropdowns that work together.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = [
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ];

  let dropdown1_selectedId = "0";
  let dropdown2_selectedId = "1";

  const formatSelected = (id) =>
    items.find((item) => item.id === id)?.text ?? "N/A";

  $: primary = formatSelected(dropdown1_selectedId);
  $: secondary = formatSelected(dropdown2_selectedId);
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <Dropdown
    labelText="Primary contact"
    helperText="Primary: {primary}"
    bind:selectedId={dropdown1_selectedId}
    {items}
  />
  <Dropdown
    invalid={dropdown1_selectedId === dropdown2_selectedId}
    invalidText="Secondary contact method must be different from the primary contact"
    labelText="Secondary contact"
    helperText="Secondary: {secondary}"
    bind:selectedId={dropdown2_selectedId}
    {items}
  />
</Stack>
```

### Events

Respond to selection, clearing, and menu-close interactions.

#### Select

Use `on:select` to listen for a new selection. The event detail includes the selected item's id and the full item.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  labelText="Contact"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  on:select={(e) => {
    console.log(e.detail.selectedId);
    console.log(e.detail.selectedItem);
  }}
/>
```

#### Clear

Use `on:clear` to listen for the selection being cleared, either via the clear button or the Delete/Backspace shortcut. Only fires when `clearable` is `true`. The event detail is the original `KeyboardEvent` or `MouseEvent`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  clearable
  selectedId="0"
  labelText="Contact"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  on:clear={(e) => console.log(e)}
/>
```

#### Close

Use `on:close` to know when the menu closes and why. `event.detail.trigger` is `"escape-key"`, `"outside-click"`, or `"select"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  labelText="Contact"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  on:close={(e) => console.log(e.detail.trigger)}
/>
```

Set `type` to `"inline"` to display the dropdown inline with other content. This variant removes the background and border.

```svelte

<Dropdown
```

### Fluid

Set `fluid` to `true` to use the fluid variant, which embeds the label inside the field. Fluid dropdowns can be used standalone or inside [FluidForm](/components/FluidForm), where the fluid variant is applied automatically. The fluid variant cannot be combined with the inline variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  fluid
  labelText="Contact"
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Dropdown, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<Dropdown
  fluid
  labelText="Contact"
  selectedId="0"
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
>
  <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
    Contact
    <TooltipIcon
      tooltipText="Your contact method is used for account notifications."
      icon={Information}
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
</Dropdown>
```

#### Condensed

By default, the fluid variant renders taller menu items to match the taller field. Set `condensed` to `true` to render menu items at their default height instead.

```svelte
<script>

<Dropdown
```

### Form name

Set `name` so the selection participates in native form submission (for example SvelteKit form actions and `FormData`). A hidden input mirrors `selectedId`, submitting an empty string when nothing is selected or when the selected item is disabled.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Form, Dropdown, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form method="POST" action="?/contact">
  <Dropdown
    name="contactMethod"
    labelText="Contact"
    items={[
      { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
      { id: "1", text: "Email" },
      { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
    ]}
  />
  <Button type="submit">Submit</Button>
</Form>
```

### Skeleton

Display a loading state using the dropdown skeleton.

```svelte
<script>
  import { DropdownSkeleton } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<DropdownSkeleton />
```
