### Closing

Control how the modal can be dismissed.

#### Prevent default

The modal dispatches a cancelable `close` event. Call `e.preventDefault()` to keep the modal open. The event includes a `trigger` property indicating what triggered the close attempt: `"escape-key"` (<kbd>Escape</kbd>), `"outside-click"`, `"close-button"`, or `"programmatic"` (the `open` prop was set to `false` from outside the component, for example through `bind:open`, rather than through one of the modal's own dismiss controls).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, InlineNotification, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
  let hasUnsavedChanges = true;
  let showWarning = false;
</script>

<Button
  on:click={() => {
    open = true;
    hasUnsavedChanges = true;
    showWarning = false;
  }}
>
  Open modal with unsaved changes
</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Edit profile"
  primaryButtonText="Save"
  secondaryButtonText="Discard changes"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => {
    hasUnsavedChanges = false;
    open = false;
  }}
  on:close={(e) => {
    console.log("Close triggered by:", e.detail.trigger);
    if (hasUnsavedChanges) {
      e.preventDefault();
      showWarning = true;
    }
  }}
  on:submit={() => {
    hasUnsavedChanges = false;
    open = false;
  }}
>
  {#if showWarning}
    <InlineNotification
      kind="warning"
      title="Unsaved changes"
      subtitle="Please save or discard your changes before closing."
      hideCloseButton
    />
  {/if}
  <p>You have unsaved changes. Click "Save" to apply them.</p>
</Modal>
```

#### Prevent on outside click

Disable closing the modal when clicking outside with `preventCloseOnClickOutside`. This is useful for transactional modals where explicit user action is required.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Create database</Button>

<Modal
  preventCloseOnClickOutside
  bind:open
  modalHeading="Create database"
  primaryButtonText="Confirm"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary
  on:open
  on:close
  on:submit
>
  <p>Create a new Cloudant database in the US South region.</p>
</Modal>
```

#### Hide close button

Set `hideCloseButton` to `true` to remove the header close button. Use this for forced-choice dialogs such as auth walls or terms acceptance. Always provide an alternative dismiss path, typically footer actions, and pair with `preventCloseOnClickOutside` when outside clicks should not dismiss the dialog. <kbd>Escape</kbd> still closes the modal unless you cancel the `close` event.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Modal } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Button on:click={() => (open = true)}>Review terms</Button>

<Modal
  bind:open
  hideCloseButton
  preventCloseOnClickOutside
  modalHeading="Accept terms of use"
  primaryButtonText="Accept"
  secondaryButtonText="Decline"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  on:submit={() => (open = false)}
>
  <p>
    You must accept or decline the terms. The header close button is hidden, so
    use the footer actions to leave this dialog.
  </p>
</Modal>
```

### Events

Modal dispatches events for its lifecycle and button interactions. Only the close button, <kbd>Escape</kbd>, and (by default) an outside click close the modal automatically. See [Closing](#closing) above. Every other action leaves `open` untouched; handle the event and set `open` to `false` yourself when the action should dismiss the dialog.

#### Open

Listen for `on:open` to know when the modal has become visible and focus has moved into it.

```svelte
<Modal bind:open on:open={() => console.log("opened")}>
```

#### Submit and button clicks

The primary button dispatches both `submit` and `click:button--primary` when clicked. Secondary buttons dispatch `click:button--secondary` with the button's `text`.

```svelte
<Modal
  bind:open
  primaryButtonText="Confirm"
  secondaryButtonText="Cancel"
  on:click:button--secondary={() => (open = false)}
  on:submit={() => (open = false)}
>
```

When `shouldSubmitOnEnter` is `true` (the default), pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> also dispatches `submit` and `click:button--primary`, unless focus is on a button, textarea, select, or contenteditable element. Set `shouldSubmitOnEnter` to `false` to disable this.

#### Transition end

Listen for `on:transitionend` to know when the modal's open or close animation finishes. `event.detail.open` reflects the modal's state at the end of the transition.

```svelte
<Modal
  bind:open
  on:transitionend={(e) => console.log("open:", e.detail.open)}
>
```

---

### Component API

#### `Modal` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the modal. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLDivElement` | Obtain a reference to the top-level HTML element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "lg"` | Set the size of the modal. | _undefined_ |
| `danger` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the danger variant | `false` |
| `alert` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable alert mode | `false` |
| `passiveModal` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the passive variant | `false` |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to remove the modal body padding so content spans edge to edge | `false` |
| `modalHeading` | `string` | Specify the modal heading. | _undefined_ |
| `modalLabel` | `string` | Specify the modal label. | _undefined_ |
| `modalAriaLabel` | `string` | Specify the ARIA label for the modal. | _undefined_ |
| `iconDescription` | `string` | Specify the ARIA label for the close icon | `"Close the modal"` |
| `hasForm` | `boolean` | Set to `true` if the modal contains form elements | `false` |
| `formId` | `string` | Specify the ID of a form element to associate with the primary button.<br />This enables the primary button to submit the form from outside the form element. | _undefined_ |
| `hasScrollingContent` | `boolean` | Set to `true` if the modal contains scrolling content | `false` |
| `primaryButtonText` | `string` | Specify the primary button text | `""` |
| `primaryButtonDisabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the primary button | `false` |
| `primaryButtonLoading` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to show a loading state on the primary button.<br />While loading, the button is non-interactive and submit is suppressed. | `false` |
| `primaryButtonLoadingDescription` | `string` | Specify the description for the primary button loading state.<br />Passed to `InlineLoading` as `description`. | `"Loading"` |
| `primaryButtonIcon` | `Icon` | Specify the primary button icon. | _undefined_ |
| `shouldSubmitOnEnter` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for the "submit" and "click:button--primary" events<br />to be dispatched when pressing "Enter". | `true` |
| `secondaryButtonText` | `string` | Specify the secondary button text | `""` |
| `secondaryButtons` | `ReadonlyArray<{ text: string; kind?: string; disabled?: boolean }>` | One or two secondary buttons for the modal footer.<br />Supersedes `secondaryButtonText`. Each entry needs `text`; optional<br />`kind` (defaults to `"secondary"`) and `disabled` pass through to Button.<br />With two entries plus a primary button, the footer uses the three-button layout. | `[]` |
| `selectorPrimaryFocus` | `string` | Specify a selector to be focused when opening the modal | `"[data-modal-primary-focus]"` |
| `preventCloseOnClickOutside` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to prevent the modal from closing when clicking outside | `false` |
| `hideCloseButton` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to hide the header close button.<br />Provide an alternative dismiss path (footer actions or Escape). | `false` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the top-level element | `uniqueId()` |

#### `Modal` slots

| Slot      | Detail                  |
| --------- | ----------------------- |
| `default` | `Record<string, never>` |
| `heading` | `Record<string, never>` |
| `label`   | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `Modal` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:keydown`    |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `Modal` dispatched events

| Event | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `on:click:button--primary` | `null` |
| `on:click:button--secondary` | `{<br />  text: string;<br />}` |
| `on:close` | `{<br />  trigger:<br />    \| "escape-key"<br />    \| "outside-click"<br />    \| "close-button"<br />    \| "programmatic";<br />}` |
| `on:open` | `null` |
| `on:submit` | `null` |
| `on:transitionend` | `{<br />  open: boolean;<br />}` |

#### `Modal` $$restProps

`Modal` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## MultiSelect

### Basic

Create a basic multi-select dropdown with three contact methods. Every item must have a unique id. By default, items are ordered alphabetically.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Content

Customize how items render and what supporting text appears around the field.

#### Custom slot

Override the default slot to customize item rendering. Use `let:item`, `let:index`, `let:selected`, and `let:highlighted` to access each item's data and its derived selected and highlighted state.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  let:item
  let:index
  let:selected
  let:highlighted
>
  <div>
    <strong>{item.text}</strong>
  </div>
  <div>
    id: {item.id} - index: {index} - selected: {selected} - highlighted:
    {highlighted}
  </div>
</MultiSelect>

<style>
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item),
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item__option) {
    height: auto;
  }

  :global(.bx--checkbox-label-text) {
    display: block;
  }
</style>
```

#### Display text

Format the display text of items using the `itemToString` prop. This example appends the item ID in parentheses.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  itemToString={(item) => {
    return item.text + " (" + item.id + ")";
  }}
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  sortItem={() => {}}
/>

### Helper text Add descriptive text below the multi-select using the
`helperText` prop.

<MultiSelect
  helperText="Select one or more contact methods"
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>

### Hidden label Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The
label remains available to screen readers.

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  hideLabel
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>

### Title attribute Set `useTitleInItem` to `true` to add a native `title`
attribute to each option, using the resolved `itemToString` text. This surfaces
a browser tooltip when an item's label is truncated by the field width.

<MultiSelect
  useTitleInItem
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>

### Checkbox values `MultiSelect` mounts a hidden `<input />` for every selected
item, derived from the current selection -- not from what's rendered in the
dropdown. This keeps native form submission (`FormData`) working while the menu
is closed, while filtering, and with `virtualize`. By default, each hidden input
uses `name={item.id}` and an empty `value`, matching the option checkbox's own
defaults. Use `itemToInput` to override `name`/`value` per item, or set the
`name` prop to give every hidden input a shared group name (unless `itemToInput`
returns its own `name`). `name` is only used for the hidden inputs -- with
`filterable`, the visible text input is a query box and is never included in
`FormData`.
```

```js
itemToInput={(item) => {
  return {
    name: 'contact',
    value: item.id
  }
}}
```

The above function sets every hidden input's name to `contact` and its value to the respective item's id, so a submission looks like `contact=0&contact=1`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  itemToInput={(item) => ({ name: "contact", value: item.id })}
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Form, MultiSelect, Button } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Form method="POST" action="?/subscribe">
  <MultiSelect
    name="contact"
    labelText="Contact"
    label="Select contact methods..."
    items={[
      { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
      { id: "1", text: "Email" },
      { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
    ]}
  />
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</Form>
```

### Selection

Control which items start selected, how selections reorder the list, and how to read the resolved order. Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> while clicking an item to select every item between it and the last item clicked.

#### Initial selection

Pre-select items by passing an array of item IDs to `selectedIds`. This example pre-selects Slack and Email.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  selectedIds={["0", "1"]}
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Selection feedback

Move selected items to the top of the list immediately after selection by setting `selectionFeedback` to `"top"`. The default behavior (top-after-reopen) only reorders items when the dropdown is reopened.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  selectionFeedback="top"
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Maximum selection

Limit how many items a user can select by setting `maxSelectedItems`. Once the cap is reached, remaining unchecked items are disabled until a selection is cleared. Select-all is unavailable when a cap is set.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  maxSelectedItems={3}
  labelText="Preferences"
  label="Select preferences..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Email" },
    { id: "1", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "2", text: "SMS" },
    { id: "3", text: "Push" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Select all

Add a "select all" item by setting isSelectAll to true on an item. Clicking this item selects or deselects all non-disabled items. Disabled items are not affected by "select all".

The select-all option is styled differently from regular options (with a separator border) so it is visually distinct as a group toggle. Its checkbox supports an `indeterminate` state when only a subset of non-disabled items are selected; it shows checked when all are selected and unchecked when none are selected.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  filterable
  labelText="Roles"
  placeholder="Filter roles..."
  items={[
    { id: "select-all", text: "All roles", isSelectAll: true },
    { id: "editor", text: "Editor" },
    { id: "owner", text: "Owner" },
    { id: "uploader", text: "Uploader" },
    { id: "reader", text: "Reader", disabled: true },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Sorted items

Bind to `sortedItems` to read the resolved list after sorting and selection feedback is applied. This avoids recomputing the order from items, selectedIds, and sortItem in consumer code.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let sortedItems = [];
</script>

<MultiSelect
  selectionFeedback="top"
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  bind:sortedItems
/>

<pre>{JSON.stringify(sortedItems, null, 2)}</pre>
```

#### Locale

Set `locale` to a BCP 47 language tag to control how the default `sortItem` orders items. The default sort uses `Intl.Collator` with numeric-aware comparison, so locale affects the ordering of accented characters and numbers embedded in text. Only used when `sortItem` is left at its default -- a custom `sortItem` ignores `locale`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  locale="de-DE"
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Öl" },
    { id: "1", text: "Apfel" },
    { id: "2", text: "Zebra" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### No alphabetical ordering

Prevent automatic alphabetical ordering by passing a no-op function to `sortItem`. This maintains the original order of items.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
  sortItem={() => {}}
/>
```

### Filterable

Enable filtering by setting `filterable` to `true`. This example includes a placeholder text for the filter input.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  spellcheck="false"
  filterable
  labelText="Contact"
  placeholder="Filter contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Fuzzy filter

Provide a custom `filterItem` to override the default substring matching. This example reuses the built-in `fuzzyMatch` utility, exported from `carbon-components-svelte`, as the predicate. It matches items whose text contains the typed characters in order (for example, "bl" matches "Blueberry" and "Blackberry"). Only the `matched` boolean is used here; the `score` and `indices` it also returns rank and highlight matches, as shown in [Highlight matches](#highlight-matches) below.

```svelte
<script>
  import { fuzzyMatch, MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  // Reuse the built-in fuzzy matcher as the filter predicate. Each typed
  // character must appear in order within the item text, so "bl" matches
  // "Blueberry" and "Blackberry". Only the `matched` boolean is used here.
  const filterItem = (item, value) => fuzzyMatch(item.text, value).matched;
</script>

<MultiSelect
  filterable
  {filterItem}
  labelText="Item"
  placeholder="Filter items..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Apple" },
    { id: "1", text: "Apricot" },
    { id: "2", text: "Banana" },
    { id: "3", text: "Blueberry" },
    { id: "4", text: "Blackberry" },
    { id: "5", text: "Cherry" },
    { id: "6", text: "Cranberry" },
    { id: "7", text: "Grape" },
    { id: "8", text: "Mango" },
    { id: "9", text: "Pineapple" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Highlight matches

Besides `matched`, `fuzzyMatch` returns the `indices` of the characters that matched. Pass them to the `highlightSegments` utility (also exported from `carbon-components-svelte`) to split the item text into matched and unmatched runs, then bold the matched runs in the default slot. Bind `value` to read the filter text inside the slot.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    fuzzyMatch,
    highlightSegments,
    MultiSelect,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";

  const items = [
    { id: "0", text: "Apple" },
    { id: "1", text: "Apricot" },
    { id: "2", text: "Banana" },
    { id: "3", text: "Blueberry" },
    { id: "4", text: "Blackberry" },
    { id: "5", text: "Cherry" },
    { id: "6", text: "Cranberry" },
    { id: "7", text: "Grape" },
    { id: "8", text: "Mango" },
    { id: "9", text: "Pineapple" },
  ];

  // One matcher drives filtering and highlighting. `filterItem` keeps the
  // items whose text fuzzy-matches the filter value; the default slot reuses
  // the same match and bolds the characters that matched. Bind `value` to read
  // the filter text inside the slot.
  const filterItem = (item, value) => fuzzyMatch(item.text, value).matched;
</script>

<MultiSelect
  bind:value
  filterable
  {filterItem}
  labelText="Item"
  placeholder="Filter items..."
  {items}
  let:item
>
  {#each highlightSegments(item.text, fuzzyMatch(item.text, value).indices) as segment}
    {#if segment.match}
      <strong>{segment.text}</strong>
    {:else}
      {segment.text}
    {/if}
  {/each}
</MultiSelect>
```

### Multiple multi-selects

Manage multiple dropdowns in a form with coordinated state.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = [
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ];

  let multiselect1_selectedIds = ["0"];
  let multiselect2_selectedIds = ["1", "2"];

  const formatSelected = (i) =>
    i.length === 0
      ? "N/A"
      : i.map((id) => items.find((item) => item.id === id).text).join(", ");

  $: primary = formatSelected(multiselect1_selectedIds);
  $: secondary = formatSelected(multiselect2_selectedIds);
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <MultiSelect
    labelText="Primary contact"
    helperText="Primary: {primary}"
    bind:selectedIds={multiselect1_selectedIds}
    label="Select contact methods..."
    {items}
  />
  <MultiSelect
    labelText="Secondary contact"
    helperText="Secondary: {secondary}"
    bind:selectedIds={multiselect2_selectedIds}
    label="Select contact methods..."
    {items}
  />
</Stack>
```

### Virtualization

Virtualization renders only the items currently visible in the viewport, improving performance for large lists. By default, the multi-select virtualizes lists with more than 100 items.

#### Large lists

In the example below, 10,000 items are provided to the multi-select but only 11 items (8 visible items + 3 overscan items) are rendered in the DOM.

Set `virtualize={false}` to explicitly disable virtualization, even for large lists. Or, customize the threshold at which virtualization activates. See [Custom threshold](#custom-threshold).

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Item ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedIds = [1000];
  $: selectedItems = items.filter((item) => selectedIds.includes(item.id));
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <MultiSelect
    filterable
    labelText="Virtualized MultiSelect (10,000 items)"
    {items}
    bind:selectedIds
  />
  <div>
    <strong>Selected:</strong>
    {selectedItems.map((item) => item.text).join(", ")}
  </div>
</Stack>
```

#### Load more

`scrollend` fires when the menu is scrolled near the bottom so you can append the next page of `items`. Same pattern as [ComboBox load more](/components/ComboBox#load-more): handle `on:scrollend`, keep prior items visible while loading, and track in-flight status locally (or with the `empty` slot when appropriate). The event is a near-bottom load-more signal, not the browser's native `scrollend`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect {items} on:scrollend={() => loadNextPage()} />
```

#### Custom overscan

Overscanning is the process of rendering extra items above and below the viewport to ensure smooth scrolling. The default overscan value is 3.

Specify a custom value for `overscan` to control how many extra items are rendered above/below the viewport for smoother scrolling.

During very fast scrolling, higher overscan values may cause more flickering due to increased DOM updates. For fast-scrolling scenarios, use a lower overscan value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Item ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedIds = [1000];
</script>

<MultiSelect
  virtualize={{ overscan: 100 }}
  filterable
  labelText="High overscan (10,000 items, overscan: 100)"
  {items}
  bind:selectedIds
/>
```

#### Custom threshold

The threshold is the minimum number of items required before virtualization activates. The default threshold value is 100, meaning lists with fewer than 100 items will not be virtualized and all items will be rendered normally.

Specify a custom value for `threshold` to control when virtualization activates. Below the threshold, all items are rendered normally without virtualization.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 100 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Item ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedIds = [50];
</script>

<MultiSelect
  virtualize={{ threshold: 200 }}
  filterable
  labelText="Custom threshold (threshold: 200)"
  {items}
  bind:selectedIds
/>
```

#### Custom item height

By default, item height matches the menu row for each size: 24px (xs), 32px (sm), 40px (md), 48px (lg, xl). Set `itemHeight` when custom slots change row height.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const items = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i,
    text: `Item ${i + 1}`,
    description: `Description for item ${i + 1}`,
  }));

  let selectedIds = [1000];
</script>

<MultiSelect
  virtualize={{ itemHeight: 60 }}
  filterable
  labelText="Custom item height (60px)"
  {items}
  bind:selectedIds
  let:item
>
  <Stack gap={2}>
    <strong>{item.text}</strong>
    <span>{item.description}</span>
  </Stack>
</MultiSelect>

<style>
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item),
  :global(.bx--list-box__menu-item__option) {
    height: auto;
  }

  :global(.bx--checkbox-label-text) {
    display: block;
  }
</style>
```

### Wrapped options

Option labels are truncated to one line. At a 320px viewport, that hides text and can leave two options looking identical, a WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow failure.

Set `wrapOptions` to let a label take as many lines as it needs. Lines break between words, and mid-word only when a word is too long to fit a line by itself. Default slot markup wraps with the label: a [highlighted match](#highlight-matches) stays marked across the break it is split by.

It defaults to `false` because wrapping changes option heights.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const roles = [
    "Chief Accessibility Officer for Regional Operations and Strategic Partnerships",
    "Deputy Director of Interdepartmental Communications and Outreach",
  ];

  const items = [
    { id: "all", text: "Select every role listed below", isSelectAll: true },
    { id: "0", text: roles[0] },
    { id: "1", text: roles[1] },
    { id: "2", text: "Analyst" },
  ];

  // Past the count at which a list is windowed, so only the options on screen
  // are rendered. `wrapOptions` turns on measured row heights by itself, so
  // offsets follow the heights the wrapped options actually take.
  const manyItems = Array.from({ length: 300 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: String(i),
    text: `${i + 1}. ${roles[i % 2]}`,
  }));

  // Input order, so the "select all" row stays in front of the roles it
  // toggles rather than sorting into the middle of them.
  const sortItem = () => 0;
</script>

<Stack gap={6} style="max-width: 20rem;">
  <MultiSelect
    labelText="Truncated (default)"
    selectedIds={["2"]}
    {sortItem}
    {items}
  />
  <MultiSelect
    wrapOptions
    labelText="Wrapped"
    selectedIds={["2"]}
    {sortItem}
    {items}
  />
  <MultiSelect
    wrapOptions
    filterable
    labelText="Wrapped (windowed, 300 items)"
    placeholder="Filter..."
    {sortItem}
    items={manyItems}
  />
</Stack>
```

### Sizes

The `size` prop sets the field height. The default is medium.

```svelte
  labelText="Contact"
```

```svelte
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Fluid

Set `fluid` to `true` to use the fluid variant, which embeds the label inside the field. Fluid multi-selects can be used standalone or inside [FluidForm](/components/FluidForm), where the fluid variant is applied automatically.

#### Filterable

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon.

```svelte
<script>

<MultiSelect
  fluid

    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },

>

    Contact
    <TooltipIcon
      tooltipText="Your contact methods are used for account notifications."
      icon={Information}
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
</MultiSelect>
```

### Portal menu

Set `portalMenu` to `true` to render the dropdown menu in a floating portal. This prevents the menu from being clipped by parent containers with `overflow: hidden` or z-index stacking contexts. Without `portalMenu`, the dropdown in the example below would be clipped by its container's hidden overflow.

When inside a [Modal](/components/Modal#modal-with-dropdowns), portalMenu defaults to true unless explicitly set to false.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack
  gap={4}
  style="overflow: hidden; border: 1px dashed var(--cds-border-subtle); padding: 1rem; max-height: 120px;"
>
  <div>
    This container has hidden overflow. Without <code>portalMenu</code>, the
    dropdown would be clipped.
  </div>
  <MultiSelect
    portalMenu
    labelText="Notification methods"
    label="Select methods..."
    items={[
      { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
      { id: "1", text: "Email" },
      { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
    ]}
  />
</Stack>
```

### States

Surface validation and interaction states. Invalid and warning states each have a filterable counterpart.

#### Invalid

Indicate an invalid selection by setting `invalid` to `true`. This example shows a required field error.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  invalid
  invalidText="A contact method is required"
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Invalid (filterable)

Combine `filterable` and `invalid` to show validation errors on a filterable multi-select.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  filterable
  invalid
  invalidText="A contact method is required"
  labelText="Contact"
  placeholder="Filter contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Warning

Indicate a warning state by setting `warn` to `true`. This example shows a warning about unassociated accounts.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  warn
  warnText="One or more contact methods are not associated with your account"
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Warning (filterable)

Combine `filterable` and `warn` to show warnings on a filterable multi-select.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  filterable
  warn
  warnText="One or more contact methods are not associated with your account"
  labelText="Contact"
  placeholder="Filter contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Disabled

Disable the entire dropdown by setting `disabled` to `true`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  disabled
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Disabled items

Disable specific items using the disabled property in the items array. This example disables the Email option.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email", disabled: true },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

#### Read-only

Set `readonly` to `true` to display non-editable values. The menu can still be opened and navigated to review the selected values, but the selection cannot be changed or cleared.

```svelte
<script>
  import { MultiSelect } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<MultiSelect
  readonly
  selectedIds={["0", "1"]}
  labelText="Contact"
  label="Select contact methods..."
  items={[
    { id: "0", text: "Slack" },
    { id: "1", text: "Email" },
    { id: "2", text: "Fax" },
  ]}
/>
```

## NotificationQueue

### Basic

Use `bind:this` to get a queue reference, then call `add()` to show notifications. The queue uses underlying [ToastNotification](ToastNotification) components, manages positioning, and removes notifications when they time out or are closed.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NotificationQueue,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={queue} />

<ButtonSet>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        kind: "success",
        title: "Success",
        subtitle: "Your changes have been saved.",
        timeout: 3000,
      });
    }}
  >
    Show success
  </Button>
  <Button
    kind="tertiary"
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        kind: "error",
        title: "Error",
        subtitle: "An error occurred while processing your request.",
        timeout: 3000,
      });
    }}
  >
    Show error
  </Button>
  <Button
    kind="tertiary"
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        kind: "info",
        title: "Information",
        subtitle: "New updates are available.",
        timeout: 3000,
      });
    }}
  >
    Show info
  </Button>
  <Button
    kind="tertiary"
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        kind: "warning",
        title: "Warning",
        subtitle: "This is a warning notification.",
        timeout: 3000,
      });
    }}
  >
    Show warning
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>
```

### Positioning

Configure where the queue and its notifications render on screen.

#### Screen position

Configure queue position with the `position` prop. Supported values are `top-left`, `top-center`, `top-right` (default), `bottom-left`, `bottom-center`, and `bottom-right`.

The top-right position assumes usage of the [UIShell](/components/UIShell) component. Use left or center placements when a side panel would otherwise cover toasts. Customize placement with [offset props](#custom-offsets).

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NotificationQueue,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let topRightQueue;
  let topCenterQueue;
  let topLeftQueue;
  let bottomRightQueue;
  let bottomCenterQueue;
  let bottomLeftQueue;
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={topRightQueue} position="top-right" />
<NotificationQueue bind:this={topCenterQueue} position="top-center" />
<NotificationQueue bind:this={topLeftQueue} position="top-left" />
<NotificationQueue bind:this={bottomRightQueue} position="bottom-right" />
<NotificationQueue bind:this={bottomCenterQueue} position="bottom-center" />
<NotificationQueue bind:this={bottomLeftQueue} position="bottom-left" />

<ButtonSet>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      topLeftQueue.add({
        kind: "info",
        title: "Top left",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add top left
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      topCenterQueue.add({
        kind: "success",
        title: "Top center",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add top center
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      topRightQueue.add({
        kind: "success",
        title: "Top right",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add top right
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>
<br />
<ButtonSet>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      bottomLeftQueue.add({
        kind: "warning",
        title: "Bottom left",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add bottom left
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      bottomCenterQueue.add({
        kind: "info",
        title: "Bottom center",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add bottom center
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      bottomRightQueue.add({
        kind: "info",
        title: "Bottom right",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add bottom right
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>
```

#### Custom offsets

Customize queue placement with `offsetTop`, `offsetBottom`, `offsetLeft`, and `offsetRight`. Useful for positioning notifications below headers or adjusting spacing.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, NotificationQueue } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
</script>

<NotificationQueue
  bind:this={queue}
  position="top-right"
  offsetTop="5rem"
  offsetRight="2rem"
/>

<Button
  on:click={() => {
    queue.add({
      kind: "success",
      title: "Custom offset",
    });
  }}
>
  Add notification
</Button>
```

#### Z-index

Specify the stacking order of the queue with `zIndex`. Defaults to `9000`, matching the z-index used by [Modal](/components/Modal), so notifications render above dialog content by default.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NotificationQueue } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NotificationQueue zIndex={2000} />
```

Lower the value if the queue should render behind other fixed UI instead.

### Managing notifications

The queue tracks notifications by id, so `add`, `update`, `remove`, and the `maxNotifications` limit all key off the same identifier.

#### Deduplication

By default, id is optional; a unique id is generated for each notification. The queue [keys](https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/each#Keyed-each-blocks) notifications by id for performance.

Notifications are deduplicated by id. Adding a notification with an id that already exists in the queue is ignored. To change an existing notification in place, use [update](#update).

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NotificationQueue,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
  let count = 0;
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={queue} />

<ButtonSet>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        id: "id",
        kind: "warning",
        title: "Duplicate notification",
        subtitle:
          "This notification has the same id. Click the button multiple times.",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add duplicate
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        id: `id-${count++}`,
        kind: "info",
        title: "Unique notification",
        subtitle: "This has a unique id, so it will always appear.",
      });
    }}
  >
    Add unique
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>
```

#### Update

Use `update(id, patch)` to change an existing notification in place. The patch merges into the matching notification, useful for reflecting progress (for example, transitioning a loading toast to success without removing and re-adding it).

`update` returns true if a notification with the given id was found, false otherwise.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, NotificationQueue } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={queue} />

<Button
  on:click={() => {
    const id = queue.add({
      id: "upload",
      kind: "info",
      title: "Uploading...",
      subtitle: "0%",
      hideCloseButton: true,
    });

    let progress = 0;
    const interval = setInterval(() => {
      progress += 25;
      if (progress < 100) {
        queue.update(id, { subtitle: `${progress}%` });
      } else {
        clearInterval(interval);
        queue.update(id, {
          kind: "success",
          title: "Upload complete",
          subtitle: "All files have been uploaded.",
          hideCloseButton: false,
          timeout: 3000,
        });
      }
    }, 600);
  }}
>
  Start upload
</Button>
```

#### Max notifications

By default, the queue displays a maximum of 3 notifications. When the limit is exceeded, the oldest notification is removed automatically.

Customize the limit with `maxNotifications`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, NotificationQueue } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
  let count = 0;
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={queue} maxNotifications={5} />

<Button
  on:click={() => {
    count++;
    queue.add({
      kind: "success",
      title: `Notification ${count}`,
    });
  }}
>
  Add notification
</Button>
```

#### Remove and clear

Use `remove(id)` to programmatically remove a specific notification, or `clear()` to remove all notifications at once.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NotificationQueue,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
  let notificationIds = [];
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={queue} />

<ButtonSet>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      const id = queue.add({
        kind: "info",
        title: "Removable notification",
        subtitle: "This notification can be removed programmatically.",
        timeout: 0,
      });
      notificationIds = [...notificationIds, id];
    }}
  >
    Add notification
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      if (notificationIds.length > 0) {
        const id = notificationIds[notificationIds.length - 1];
        queue.remove(id);
        notificationIds = notificationIds.slice(0, -1);
      }
    }}
  >
    Remove last
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.clear();
      notificationIds = [];
    }}
  >
    Clear all
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>
```

### Persistent

Create persistent notifications that do not auto-dismiss by omitting timeout and hiding the close button with `hideCloseButton`.

These notifications remain visible until programmatically removed.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NotificationQueue,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let queue;
</script>

<NotificationQueue bind:this={queue} />

<ButtonSet>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        kind: "warning",
        title: "Persistent notification",
        subtitle:
          "This notification has no close button and will not auto-dismiss.",
        hideCloseButton: true,
      });
    }}
  >
    Add persistent
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.add({
        kind: "info",
        title: "Auto-dismiss notification",
        subtitle:
          "This notification has no close button but will auto-dismiss after 3 seconds.",
        hideCloseButton: true,
        timeout: 3000,
      });
    }}
  >
    Add auto-dismiss
  </Button>
  <Button
    on:click={() => {
      queue.clear();
    }}
  >
    Clear all
  </Button>
</ButtonSet>
```

---

### Component API

#### `NotificationQueue` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `"top-left" \| "top-center" \| "top-right" \| "bottom-left" \| "bottom-center" \| "bottom-right"` | Specify the position of the notification queue. | `"top-right"` |
| `offsetTop` | `string` | Specify the top offset (CSS value) | `"3rem"` |
| `offsetBottom` | `string` | Specify the bottom offset (CSS value) | `"1rem"` |
| `offsetLeft` | `string` | Specify the left offset (CSS value) | `"1rem"` |
| `offsetRight` | `string` | Specify the right offset (CSS value) | `"1rem"` |
| `zIndex` | `number` | Specify the z-index of the notification queue.<br />By default, this matches the z-index of modals. | `9000` |
| `maxNotifications` | `number` | Specify the maximum number of notifications to display.<br />When this limit is exceeded, the oldest notification is automatically removed. | `3` |
| `add` | `(notification: NotificationData) => string` | Add a notification to the queue.<br />If a notification with the same id already exists, the call is ignored.<br />To change an existing notification in place, use `update`.<br />Returns the notification id (either the provided id or a generated one). | _undefined_ |
| `update` | `(id: string, patch: Partial<NotificationData>) => boolean` | Update an existing notification by id, merging `patch` into it.<br />The id of the notification cannot be changed.<br />Returns true if the notification was found and updated, false otherwise. | _undefined_ |
| `remove` | `(id: string) => boolean` | Remove a notification by id.<br />Returns true if the notification was found and removed, false otherwise. | _undefined_ |
| `clear` | `() => any` | Clear all notifications. | _undefined_ |

#### `NotificationQueue` typedefs

```ts
type NotificationData = {
  /** Optional id for deduplication */
  id?: string;
  kind?:
    "error" | "info" | "info-square" | "success" | "warning" | "warning-alt";
  title?: string;
  subtitle?: string;
  caption?: string;
  timeout?: number;
  lowContrast?: boolean;
  closeButtonDescription?: string;
  hideCloseButton?: boolean;
};
```


## NumberInput

### Basic

Create a basic number input with increment and decrement controls. The input accepts numerical values and provides visual feedback.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

### No value

Allow empty values by setting `allowEmpty` to `true` and `value` to `null`. Both are required: allowEmpty enables the empty state, and null represents no value.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NumberInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = null;
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <NumberInput
    labelText="Clusters"
    allowEmpty
    bind:value
    helperText="Value: {value}"
  />
  <ButtonSet>
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => (value = null)}>
      Set to null
    </Button>
    <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => (value = 0)}>
      Set to 0
    </Button>
  </ButtonSet>
</Stack>
```

### Helper text

Add descriptive text below the input with `helperText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  labelText="Clusters"
  value={0}
  helperText="Clusters provisioned in your region"
/>
```

### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput hideLabel labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to provide custom label content.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput labelText="" value={0}>
  <strong slot="labelChildren">Clusters</strong>
</NumberInput>
```

### Range and steps

Control the allowed values and increment.

#### Min and max

Constrain input values with `min` and `max`. Stepper buttons stop at the range limits. Typed values outside the range show an invalid state rather than silently clamping. Add `invalidText` for an error message.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  min={4}
  max={20}
  value={4}
  invalidText="Number must be between 4 and 20."
  helperText="Clusters provisioned in your region"
  labelText="Clusters (4 min, 20 max)"
/>
```

#### Step

Control increment and decrement step size with `step`. This example uses a step of 0.1.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  value={1}
  helperText="Step of 0.1"
  step={0.1}
  labelText="Clusters"
/>
```

#### Step start

Configure a starting point for stepping when the input is empty or zero with `stepStartValue`. When the user clicks increment or decrement, the value jumps to stepStartValue instead of stepping from zero.

This is useful when zero is outside the min/max range, or when a more sensible default exists (for example, the current year). Combined with allowEmpty, it ensures the user interacts with the input before submitting a value.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  stepStartValue={2026}
  allowEmpty
  min={2026}
  max={2100}
  labelText="Year"
/>
```

### Formatting

Control how the value is parsed and displayed.

#### Preserve decimals

Preserve decimal input formatting like `"1.0"`, `"2.00"`, or `"3."` by setting `allowDecimal` to `true`. The input uses text mode with decimal input instead of a native number field, so trailing zeros and decimal points stay intact while typing. Useful for financial data or precise decimal entry.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    ButtonSet,
    NumberInput,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = 1.5;
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <NumberInput
    allowDecimal
    allowEmpty
    bind:value
    step={0.01}
    labelText="Amount"
  />

  <ButtonSet>
    <Button on:click={() => (value = null)}>Set to null</Button>
    <Button on:click={() => (value = 0)}>Set to 0</Button>
    <Button on:click={() => (value = 1.23)}>Set to 1.23</Button>
  </ButtonSet>

  <div>
    <strong>Value:</strong>
    {value}
  </div>
</Stack>
```

#### Locale

Format numbers according to a locale with `locale` and a BCP 47 language tag. The display value is formatted on blur using Intl.NumberFormat. When locale is set, the input uses text mode with decimal input.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput locale="de-DE" value={1234.5} labelText="Amount (German)" />
```

#### Locale options

Combine `locale` with `formatOptions` for additional formatting control such as decimal precision.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  locale="en-US"
  formatOptions={{ minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 }}
  value={1234.5}
  labelText="Price"
/>
```

### Custom validation

Use `validate` for custom validation logic. The function receives the raw input string and optional locale. Return `false` to mark invalid, `true` to force valid (overriding auto bounds checks), or `undefined` to use built-in validation.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  validate={(raw) => {
    const num = Number(raw);
    return Number.isNaN(num) ? undefined : num % 2 === 0;
  }}
  invalidText="Must be an even number"
  labelText="Even number"
  value={0}
/>

## Stepper controls Control the stepper buttons and scroll-wheel interaction.
### Hidden steppers Hide the increment and decrement controls by setting
`hideSteppers` to `true`.

<NumberInput hideSteppers labelText="Clusters" value={0} />

### Disable wheel Prevent the scroll wheel from changing the input value by
setting `disableWheel` to `true`. This is useful in forms where accidental
scroll changes are undesirable.

<NumberInput disableWheel labelText="Clusters" value={0} />

## Events Respond to value changes and stepper interactions. ### Value change
Use `on:input` to listen for every keystroke, and `on:change` to listen for
committed changes--on blur, or immediately after a stepper click or arrow key
press. Both events dispatch the parsed value directly as `event.detail`.

<NumberInput
  on:input={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // number | null
  on:change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} // number | null
/>

### Blur Use `on:blur` to listen for when the input loses focus. The event
detail includes the current parsed value and the original FocusEvent.

<NumberInput
  on:blur={(e) => {
    console.log(e.detail.value); // number | null
    console.log(e.detail.event); // FocusEvent
  }}
/>

### Stepper click Use `on:click:stepper` to listen for stepper button clicks.
The event detail includes the updated value and direction (`"up"` or `"down"`).
This event only fires on button clicks, not arrow key presses.

<NumberInput
  on:click:stepper={(e) => {
    console.log(e.detail.value); // number
    console.log(e.detail.direction); // "up" | "down"
  }}
/>

### Stepper blur Use `on:blur:stepper` to listen for when a stepper button loses
focus. The event detail includes the current value, direction, and original
FocusEvent.

<NumberInput
  on:blur:stepper={(e) => {
    console.log(e.detail.value); // number | null
    console.log(e.detail.direction); // "up" | "down"
    console.log(e.detail.event); // FocusEvent
  }}
/>

### Stepper
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = 0;
  let clickStepperEvents = [];
  let blurEvents = [];
  let blurStepperEvents = [];
</script>

<Stack gap={4}>
  <NumberInput
    bind:value
    labelText="Clusters"
    on:click:stepper={(e) => {
      clickStepperEvents = [
        ...clickStepperEvents,
        `value: ${e.detail.value}, direction: ${e.detail.direction}`,
      ];
    }}
    on:blur={(e) => {
      blurEvents = [...blurEvents, `value: ${e.detail.value}`];
    }}
    on:blur:stepper={(e) => {
      blurStepperEvents = [
        ...blurStepperEvents,
        `value: ${e.detail.value}, direction: ${e.detail.direction}`,
      ];
    }}
  />
  <Stack gap={4}>
    <Stack gap={2}>
      <strong>click:stepper events:</strong>
      <pre>{clickStepperEvents.join("\n") || "(none)"}</pre>
    </Stack>
    <Stack gap={2}>
      <strong>blur events:</strong>
      <pre>{blurEvents.join("\n") || "(none)"}</pre>
    </Stack>
    <Stack gap={2}>
      <strong>blur:stepper events:</strong>
      <pre>{blurStepperEvents.join("\n") || "(none)"}</pre>
    </Stack>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

### Sizes

`size` sets the input height. The default is `"md"`.

#### Extra-large

Use the extra-large size for prominent inputs by setting `size` to `"xl"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput size="xl" labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

#### Small

Use the small size for compact layouts by setting `size` to `"sm"`. This is ideal for secondary inputs.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput size="sm" labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

### Light

Use the light variant for dark backgrounds by setting `light` to `true`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput light labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

### Fluid

Set `fluid` to `true` to use the fluid variant, which embeds the label inside the field. Fluid number inputs can be used standalone or inside [FluidForm](/components/FluidForm), where the fluid variant is applied automatically.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput fluid labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

#### Hidden steppers

The fluid variant works with `hideSteppers` to remove the increment and decrement controls.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput fluid hideSteppers labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput fluid value={0}>
  <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
    Clusters
    <TooltipIcon
      tooltipText="The number of clusters provisioned in your region."
      icon={Information}
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
</NumberInput>
```

#### Invalid

Fluid number inputs display the error message inside the field boundary. Long messages wrap to multiple lines.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  fluid
  invalid
  invalidText="The number of clusters must be between 4 and 20 to provision a highly available cluster in this region."
  labelText="Clusters"
  value={0}
/>
```

#### Warning

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<NumberInput
  fluid
  warn
  warnText="Increasing the cluster count will incur additional charges."
  labelText="Clusters"
  value={0}
/>
```

#### Disabled

Invalid and warning states are not displayed while the input is disabled.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

<NumberInput
  fluid
  disabled
  invalid
  invalidText="The number of clusters is invalid."
  labelText="Clusters"
  value={0}

```

#### Read-only

Invalid and warning states are not displayed while the input is read-only.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput } from "carbon-components-svelte";

<NumberInput fluid readonly labelText="Clusters" value={0} />
```

### Component API

#### `NumberInput` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `null \| number` | Specify the input value.<br />Use `null` to denote "no value". | `null` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLInputElement` | Obtain a reference to the input HTML element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "xl"` | Set the size of the input. | _undefined_ |
| `step` | `number` | Specify the step increment | `1` |
| `max` | `number` | Specify the maximum value. | _undefined_ |
| `min` | `number` | Specify the minimum value. | _undefined_ |
| `stepStartValue` | `number` | Provide the value stepping should begin at when the input is empty. | _undefined_ |
| `light` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable the light variant | `false` |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for the input to be read-only | `false` |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the fluid variant.<br />Inherited from the parent `FluidForm` context,<br />so it does not need to be set when used inside `FluidForm`. | `false` |
| `allowEmpty` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to allow for an empty value | `false` |
| `allowDecimal` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to preserve decimal input formatting.<br />When enabled, uses type="text" with inputmode="decimal" instead of type="number". | `false` |
| `locale` | `string` | Specify a BCP 47 locale for number formatting.<br />When set, forces type="text" with inputmode="decimal"<br />and formats the display value using Intl.NumberFormat. | _undefined_ |
| `formatOptions` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` | Specify Intl.NumberFormat options when `locale` is set. | _undefined_ |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the input | `false` |
| `hideSteppers` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to hide the input stepper buttons | `false` |
| `disableWheel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to prevent the scroll wheel from changing the input value | `false` |
| `validate` | `(value: string, locale: string \| undefined) => boolean \| undefined` | Custom validation function.<br />Receives the current raw input string and locale.<br />Return `true` to force valid, `false` to force invalid,<br />or `undefined` to defer to built-in validation. | _undefined_ |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate an invalid state | `false` |
| `invalidText` | `string` | Specify the invalid state text | `""` |
| `warn` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate a warning state | `false` |
| `warnText` | `string` | Specify the warning state text | `""` |
| `helperText` | `string` | Specify the helper text | `""` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text | `false` |
| `translateWithId` | `(id: NumberInputTranslationId) => string` | Override the default translation ids. | `(id) => defaultTranslations[id]` |
| `translationIds` | `{ increment: "increment"; decrement: "decrement" }` | Default translation ids. | `{<br />  increment: "increment",<br />  decrement: "decrement",<br />}` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the input element | `uniqueId()` |
| `name` | `string` | Specify a name attribute for the input. | _undefined_ |

#### `NumberInput` typedefs


## OrderedList

### Basic

Create a basic ordered list by wrapping list item components within the ordered list. For tree-structured data, consider [RecursiveList](/components/RecursiveList#ordered).

```svelte
<script>
  import { ListItem, OrderedList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OrderedList>
  <ListItem>Ordered list item</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Ordered list item</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Ordered list item</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
```

### With links

Add interactive elements like link components within list items.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link, ListItem, OrderedList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OrderedList>
  <ListItem>
    <Link href="#">Ordered list item</Link>
  </ListItem>
  <ListItem>
    <Link href="#">Ordered list item</Link>
  </ListItem>
  <ListItem>
    <Link href="#">Ordered list item</Link>
  </ListItem>
</OrderedList>
```

### Nested lists

Create hierarchical lists with support for the browser's native numbering style.

#### Standard

Set `nested` on a child ordered list for proper indentation and numbering.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ListItem, OrderedList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OrderedList>
  <ListItem>
    Ordered list level 1
    <OrderedList nested>
      <ListItem>Ordered list level 2</ListItem>
      <ListItem>
        Ordered list level 3
        <OrderedList nested>
          <ListItem>Ordered list level 3</ListItem>
          <ListItem>Ordered list level 3</ListItem>
        </OrderedList>
      </ListItem>
    </OrderedList>
  </ListItem>
  <ListItem>Ordered list level 1</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Ordered list level 1</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
```

#### Native styles

Set `native` to `true` to use the browser's native list styles. Useful for large lists where the list number may overlap with the list item text.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ListItem, OrderedList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OrderedList native>
  <ListItem>
    Ordered list level 1
    <OrderedList nested>
      <ListItem>Ordered list level 2</ListItem>
      <ListItem>
        Ordered list level 3
        <OrderedList nested>
          <ListItem>Ordered list level 3</ListItem>
          <ListItem>Ordered list level 3</ListItem>
        </OrderedList>
      </ListItem>
    </OrderedList>
  </ListItem>
  <ListItem>Ordered list level 1</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Ordered list level 1</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
```

### Expressive styles

Use Carbon's expressive typesetting with `expressive`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Link, ListItem, OrderedList } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OrderedList expressive>
  <ListItem><Link size="lg" href="#">Ordered list item</Link></ListItem>
  <ListItem>Ordered list item</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Ordered list item</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
```

## OverflowMenu

### Basic

Create a basic overflow menu by wrapping overflow menu item components within the overflow menu. For menus that need submenus, use [MenuButton](/components/MenuButton#icon-only) instead.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu>
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

### Reactive example

Control the menu state programmatically by binding to `open`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    OverflowMenu,
    OverflowMenuItem,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let open = false;
</script>

<Stack gap={6} align="start">
  <OverflowMenu bind:open>
    <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
    <OverflowMenuItem
      href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
      target="_blank"
      text="API documentation"
    />
    <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
  </OverflowMenu>
  <Button kind="tertiary" size="small" on:click={() => (open = !open)}>
    {open ? "Close menu" : "Open menu"}
  </Button>
</Stack>
```

### Positioning

Control where and how the menu opens.

#### Portal

Set `portalMenu` to `true` to render the menu in a floating portal, so it is not clipped by `overflow: hidden` parents or z-index stacking. Without portalling, the menu below would be clipped.

Inside a [Modal](/components/Modal), portalling is on by default unless you set `portalMenu` to `false`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    OverflowMenu,
    OverflowMenuItem,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Stack
  gap={4}
  style="overflow: hidden; border: 1px dashed var(--cds-border-subtle); padding: 1rem; max-height: 120px;"
>
  <div>
    This container has hidden overflow. Without <code>portalMenu</code>, the
    menu would be clipped.
  </div>
  <OverflowMenu portalMenu>
    <OverflowMenuItem text="Edit" />
    <OverflowMenuItem text="Duplicate" />
    <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete" />
  </OverflowMenu>
</Stack>
```

### Scrollable

Set `maxHeight` to cap the menu height and scroll the remaining items. A number is treated as pixels; a string is used as any CSS length, such as `"20rem"`. Keyboard navigation scrolls the focused item into view.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const workspaces = Array.from(
    { length: 20 },
    (_, index) => `Workspace ${index + 1}`,
  );
</script>

<OverflowMenu maxHeight={240}>
  {#each workspaces as workspace (workspace)}
    <OverflowMenuItem text={workspace} />
  {/each}
  <OverflowMenuItem hasDivider danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

### Events

Respond to menu close attempts and individual item clicks.

#### Close event

Use `on:close` to respond to every close attempt, regardless of cause. The event detail includes `trigger` (`"toggle"`, `"escape-key"`, `"outside-click"`, or `"item-select"`); when triggered by a selection, `index` and `text` identify the selected item.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<OverflowMenu
  on:close={(e) => {
    console.log(e.detail.trigger); // "toggle" | "escape-key" | "outside-click" | "item-select"
    console.log(e.detail.index); // number | undefined
    console.log(e.detail.text); // string | undefined
  }}
>
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Manage credentials" />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    href="https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/api-gateway/"
    target="_blank"
    text="API documentation"
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem danger text="Delete service" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Prevent item close

Use `e.preventDefault()` on an individual overflow menu item click event to prevent the menu from closing when that item is clicked. Use this to keep the menu open after performing an action.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let copying = false;
  let copied = false;

  async function copyToClipboard() {
    if (copying) return;
    copying = true;
    copied = false;
    await navigator.clipboard.writeText("Sample text to copy");
    copied = true;
    setTimeout(() => {
      copied = false;
    }, 2000);

    copying = false;
  }
</script>

<OverflowMenu size="field">
  <OverflowMenuItem
    text={copied ? "Copied!" : "Copy page"}
    disabled={copying}
    on:click={(e) => {
      // Prevent menu from closing for this item.
      e.preventDefault();
      copyToClipboard();
    }}
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem text="Close menu" />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### Cancel close event

The `close` event is cancelable. Call `e.preventDefault()` on it to keep the menu open when it would otherwise close from the trigger, <kbd>Escape</kbd>, or an outside click. The example below guards against accidentally dismissing unsaved changes: toggle a setting, then try to close the menu without saving.

```svelte
<script>
  import { OverflowMenu, OverflowMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let emailEnabled = false;
  let smsEnabled = false;
  let saved = true;

  function toggle(setter) {
    return (e) => {
      // Keep the menu open while editing settings.
      e.preventDefault();
      setter();
      saved = false;
    };
  }
</script>

<OverflowMenu
  on:close={(e) => {
    // Guard against accidentally dismissing unsaved changes.
    if (!saved && !window.confirm("Discard unsaved notification settings?")) {
      e.preventDefault();
    }
  }}
>
  <OverflowMenuItem
    text="Email alerts: {emailEnabled ? 'On' : 'Off'}"
    on:click={toggle(() => (emailEnabled = !emailEnabled))}
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    text="SMS alerts: {smsEnabled ? 'On' : 'Off'}"
    on:click={toggle(() => (smsEnabled = !smsEnabled))}
  />
  <OverflowMenuItem
    hasDivider
    text="Save changes"
    on:click={() => {
      // Allow the menu to close after saving.
      saved = true;
    }}
  />
</OverflowMenu>
```

#### `OverflowMenu` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true` to open the menu. | `false` |
| `icon` (Reactive) | `Icon` | Specify the icon to render. | `OverflowMenuVertical` |
| `buttonRef` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLButtonElement` | Obtain a reference to the trigger button element. | `null` |
| `menuRef` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLUListElement` | Obtain a reference to the overflow menu element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "xl"` | Specify the size of the overflow menu. | _undefined_ |
| `direction` | `"top" \| "bottom"` | Specify the direction of the overflow menu relative to the button. | `"bottom"` |
| `light` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable the light variant | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the trigger button | `false` |
| `flipped` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to flip the menu relative to the button | `false` |
| `maxHeight` | `number \| string` | Specify the maximum height of the menu.<br />A number is treated as pixels; a string is used as a CSS length.<br />The menu scrolls once its items exceed the height. | _undefined_ |
| `menuOptionsClass` | `string` | Specify the menu options class. | _undefined_ |
| `iconClass` | `string` | Specify the icon class. | _undefined_ |
| `iconDescription` | `string` | Specify the ARIA label for the icon | `"Open and close list of options"` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the button element | `uniqueId()` |
| `portalMenu` | `boolean \| undefined` | Set to `true` to render the menu in a portal,<br />allowing it to escape containers with `overflow: hidden`.<br />When inside a Modal, defaults to `true` unless explicitly set to `false`. | _undefined_ |

## Pagination

### Basic

Create a basic pagination component with default page size options. The default size is medium.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination totalItems={102} pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]} />
```

### Sizes

The default control height is medium. Set `size` to choose another variant.

#### Extra-small

Set `size` to `"xs"` to pair pagination with a compact data table.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination size="xs" totalItems={102} pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]} />
```

#### Small

Set `size` to `"sm"` for a small pagination.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination size="sm" totalItems={102} pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]} />
```

#### Large

Set `size` to `"lg"` for a large pagination.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination size="lg" totalItems={102} pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]} />
```

### Page and page size

Configure the current page, and the available and default page sizes.

#### Current page

Set the current page with `page`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination totalItems={102} page={4} />
```

#### Custom sizes

Specify custom page sizes and set a default page size.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination totalItems={102} pageSizes={[16, 36, 99]} pageSize={36} />
```

#### Dynamic sizes

Set `dynamicPageSizes` to hide page sizes larger than needed to display all items on one page.

For example, with 9 total items and page sizes of `[5, 10, 15]`, only 5 and 10 appear because 10 already exceeds the total.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination totalItems={9} pageSizes={[5, 10, 15]} dynamicPageSizes />
```

### Unknown pages

Set `pagesUnknown` when the total page count is unknown, such as with cursor-based APIs. The item range renders without a total, and the forward button is not constrained by totalItems.

Because the component cannot detect the last page, bind to `page` and toggle `forwardButtonDisabled` when there is no more data to load. The back button is disabled automatically once `page` reaches `1`; override `backButtonDisabled` the same way if the consumer needs equivalent manual control over the back button.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  // Simulate a cursor-based API where the total is unknown.
  const LAST_PAGE = 5;

  let page = 1;
  let pageSize = 10;

  $: forwardButtonDisabled = page >= LAST_PAGE;
</script>

<Pagination pagesUnknown bind:page bind:pageSize {forwardButtonDisabled} />
```

#### Custom item and page text

Because the total is unknown, this mode falls back to `itemText` and `pageText` instead of `itemRangeText` and `pageRangeText`, since there's no total to describe. Override either to change the wording.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Pagination
  pagesUnknown
  itemText={(min, max) => `Showing ${min}-${max}`}
  pageText={(page) => `Page ${page}`}
/>
```

### Page window

The page-number dropdown uses native `<option>` elements, derived from `totalItems`. For large datasets, use `pageWindow` to cap how many options are rendered (default 1000).

This example also overrides `itemRangeText` and `pageRangeText` to format the item and page counts compactly (for example, `100k` instead of `100,000`).

```svelte
<script>
  import { Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const formatNumber = (value) => {
    return Intl.NumberFormat("en", { notation: "compact" })
      .format(value)
      .toLowerCase();
  };
</script>

<Pagination
  totalItems={100_000}
  pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]}
  itemRangeText={(min, max, total) =>
    `${formatNumber(min)}-${formatNumber(max)} of ${formatNumber(total)} items`}
  pageRangeText={(_current, total) => `of ${formatNumber(total)} pages`}
/>
```

### Custom page select

Use the `pageSelect` slot to replace the default page-number `Select` with your own control. The slot exposes `currentPage`, `totalPages`, `currentPageSize`, and `selectLabelText` for display; bind `page` on `Pagination` itself and set it from within the slot to navigate.

```svelte
<script>
  import { NumberInput, Pagination } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let page = 1;
</script>

<Pagination bind:page totalItems={102} pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]}>
  <svelte:fragment slot="pageSelect" let:totalPages let:selectLabelText>
    <NumberInput
      size="sm"
      hideLabel
      hideSteppers
      labelText={selectLabelText}
      min={1}
      max={totalPages}
      bind:value={page}
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
</Pagination>
```

### Simple

Set `simple` for a compact previous/next control with page status text. Useful in toolbars and cards.

The example below also overrides `pageText` to show only the page number, omitting the default `"page "` prefix.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Pagination,
    PaginationSkeleton,
    Toolbar,
    ToolbarContent,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Toolbar size="sm">
  <ToolbarContent>
    <Pagination
      simple
      size="sm"
      totalItems={102}
      pageText={(page) => `${page.toLocaleString()}`}
    />
  </ToolbarContent>
</Toolbar>

## Custom text Override the button tooltips and items-per-page label
independently of the total and item text overrides above.

<Pagination
  totalItems={102}
  pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]}
  forwardText="Next"
  backwardText="Previous"
  itemsPerPageText="Rows per page:"
/>

## Hidden controls Hide individual pagination controls. ### Page input Disable
the page input with `pageInputDisabled`.

<Pagination totalItems={102} pageInputDisabled />

### Page size Disable the page size selector with `pageSizeInputDisabled`.

<Pagination totalItems={102} pageSizeInputDisabled />

## Disabled Set `disabled` to `true` to disable the entire pagination, including
the nav buttons and both selects.

<Pagination disabled totalItems={102} pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]} />

## Events ### Change Use `on:change` to listen for direct user interaction--the
previous/next buttons, or the page and page-size selects. The event detail
includes whichever value changed.

<Pagination
  totalItems={102}
  pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]}
  on:change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} // { page: number } | { pageSize: number }
/>

### Update Use `on:update` to listen for every change to `page` or `pageSize`,
including programmatic updates from outside the component (for example, through
`bind:page`). Unlike `change`, this fires regardless of whether the update came
from user interaction, and the detail always includes both values.

<Pagination
  totalItems={102}
  pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]}
  on:update={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} // { page: number, pageSize: number }
/>

### Button clicks Use `on:click:button--previous` and `on:click:button--next` to
listen specifically for previous and next button clicks, separate from the page
and page-size selects. Both dispatch the resulting page number.

<Pagination
  totalItems={102}
  pageSizes={[10, 15, 20]}
  on:click:button--previous={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // { page: number }
  on:click:button--next={(e) => console.log(e.detail)} // { page: number }
/>

## Skeleton Use the pagination skeleton to show a loading state.

<PaginationSkeleton />

### Extra-small Display a loading state for the extra small pagination variant.

<PaginationSkeleton size="xs" />

### Small Display a loading state for the small pagination variant.

<PaginationSkeleton size="sm" />

### Large Display a loading state for the large pagination variant.

<PaginationSkeleton size="lg" />
```
