### Component API

#### `Search` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `T` | Specify the value of the search input. | `""` |
| `expanded` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Set to `true to expand the search input. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLInputElement` | Obtain a reference to the input HTML element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | Specify the size of the search input. | `"xl"` |
| `searchClass` | `string` | Specify the class name passed to the outer div element | `""` |
| `skeleton` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to display the skeleton state | `false` |
| `light` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable the light variant | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the search input | `false` |
| `expandable` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable the expandable variant | `false` |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the fluid variant.<br />Inherited from the parent `FluidForm` context,<br />so it does not need to be set when used inside `FluidForm`.<br />Cannot be combined with the expandable variant. | `false` |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Specify the `placeholder` attribute of the search input | `"Search..."` |
| `autocomplete` | `"on" \| "off"` | Specify the `autocomplete` attribute. | `"off"` |
| `autofocus` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to auto focus the search element | `false` |
| `closeButtonLabelText` | `string` | Specify the close button label text | `"Clear search input"` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
| `icon` | `Icon` | Specify the icon to render. | `IconSearch` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the input element | `uniqueId()` |

#### `Search` slots

| Slot            | Detail                  |
| --------------- | ----------------------- |
| `labelChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `Search` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:blur`       |
| `on:change`     |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:focus`      |
| `on:input`      |
| `on:keydown`    |
| `on:keyup`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |
| `on:paste`      |

#### `Search` dispatched events

| Event         | Detail |
| ------------- | ------ |
| `on:clear`    | `null` |
| `on:collapse` | `null` |
| `on:expand`   | `null` |

#### `Search` $$restProps

`Search` spreads `$$restProps` to the `input` element.

#### `SearchSkeleton` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | Specify the size of the search input. | `"xl"` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to hide the label text | `false` |

#### `SearchSkeleton` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `SearchSkeleton` $$restProps

`SearchSkeleton` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.

#### `FluidSearchSkeleton` forwarded events

| Event           |
| --------------- |
| `on:click`      |
| `on:mouseenter` |
| `on:mouseleave` |
| `on:mouseover`  |

#### `FluidSearchSkeleton` $$restProps

`FluidSearchSkeleton` spreads `$$restProps` to the `div` element.


## SearchMenu

### Basic

Render `SearchMenuItem` children to display suggestions. Each item highlights the portion of its `text` that matches the search value. Result text is flush-left with the input placeholder. The menu opens on focus. Use the arrow keys to move between results, <kbd>Enter</kbd> to select the active result, and <kbd>Escape</kbd> to close the menu. The menu also closes on an outside click.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "Data";

  const resources = [
    { id: "svc-db-testsql", name: "Databases for TestSQL" },
    { id: "svc-att-iot", name: "AT&T IoT Data Plans" },
    { id: "svc-memcache", name: "Data Store for Memcache" },
    { id: "svc-hazardhub", name: "HazardHub Property Risk Data API" },
    { id: "svc-financial", name: "Managed Financial Data API" },
  ];
</script>

<SearchMenu bind:value labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  {#each resources as resource (resource.id)}
    <SearchMenuItem
      text={resource.name}
      value={resource.id}
      on:select={(e) => console.log("select", e.detail)}
    />
  {/each}
</SearchMenu>
```

### Sizes

The search input is extra-large (`"xl"`) by default. Set `size` to choose another variant, matching the [Search](/components/Search) input sizing. By default the results menu adjusts to match the input: row height, text inset, and the leading-icon gutter all align with the input for the chosen size.

#### Extra large

The default. Set `size` to `"xl"` for an extra-large search input.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Link,
    SearchMenu,
    SearchMenuGroup,
    SearchMenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Catalog from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Catalog.svelte";
  import DataBase from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/DataBase.svelte";
  import Launch from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Launch.svelte";

  let value = "Data";

  const resources = [
    {
      id: "res-pg-test",
      name: "Databases for PostgreSQL-Test",
      icon: DataBase,
    },
    { id: "res-memcache", name: "Data Store for Memcache", icon: DataBase },
  ];
  const catalog = [
    { id: "cat-att-iot", name: "AT&T IoT Data Plans", icon: Catalog },
    { id: "cat-financial", name: "Managed Financial Data API", icon: Catalog },
  ];
</script>

<SearchMenu size="xl" bind:value labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  <SearchMenuGroup label="Resource results">
    <Link slot="action" href="#resources">View all</Link>
    {#each resources as item (item.id)}
      <SearchMenuItem
        text={item.name}
        value={item.id}
        icon={item.icon}
        href="#resource"
      />
    {/each}
  </SearchMenuGroup>

  <SearchMenuGroup label="Catalog results">
    <Link slot="action" href="#catalog">View all</Link>
    {#each catalog as item (item.id)}
      <SearchMenuItem
        text={item.name}
        value={item.id}
        icon={item.icon}
        href="#catalog"
      />
    {/each}
  </SearchMenuGroup>

  <SearchMenuGroup divider>
    <SearchMenuItem
      persistent
      iconRight={Launch}
      href="#docs"
      text={`Search "${value}" in Docs`}
    />
  </SearchMenuGroup>
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Decoupled menu size

Set `menuSize` to size the results menu independently of the input. By default the menu follows `size`; override it when you want a compact input with a roomier menu, or vice versa. The example below pairs a small input with an extra-large menu.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Link,
    SearchMenu,
    SearchMenuGroup,
    SearchMenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Catalog from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Catalog.svelte";
  import DataBase from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/DataBase.svelte";
  import Launch from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Launch.svelte";

  let value = "Data";

  const resources = [
    {
      id: "res-pg-test",
      name: "Databases for PostgreSQL-Test",
      icon: DataBase,
    },
    { id: "res-memcache", name: "Data Store for Memcache", icon: DataBase },
  ];
  const catalog = [
    { id: "cat-att-iot", name: "AT&T IoT Data Plans", icon: Catalog },
    { id: "cat-financial", name: "Managed Financial Data API", icon: Catalog },
  ];
</script>

<!-- Compact input, roomier menu: `size` sizes the input, `menuSize` the menu. -->
<SearchMenu
  size="sm"
  menuSize="xl"
  bind:value
  labelText="Search"
  placeholder="Search..."
>
  <SearchMenuGroup label="Resource results">
    <Link slot="action" href="#resources">View all</Link>
    {#each resources as item (item.id)}
      <SearchMenuItem
        text={item.name}
        value={item.id}
        icon={item.icon}
        href="#resource"
      />
    {/each}
  </SearchMenuGroup>

  <SearchMenuGroup label="Catalog results">
    <Link slot="action" href="#catalog">View all</Link>
    {#each catalog as item (item.id)}
      <SearchMenuItem
        text={item.name}
        value={item.id}
        icon={item.icon}
        href="#catalog"
      />
    {/each}
  </SearchMenuGroup>

  <SearchMenuGroup divider>
    <SearchMenuItem
      persistent
      iconRight={Launch}
      href="#docs"
      text={`Search "${value}" in Docs`}
    />
  </SearchMenuGroup>
</SearchMenu>
```

### Grouping

Compose `SearchMenuGroup` and `SearchMenuItem` for grouped results, recent searches, and footer actions.

#### Grouped results

Wrap items in `SearchMenuGroup` to add a category header. Use the `action` slot to add a header action such as a "View all" link. Set `divider` on a group to separate footer actions, and `persistent` on an item to keep it visible regardless of the search value. Provide `icon` for a leading icon and `iconRight` for a trailing affordance.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Link,
    SearchMenu,
    SearchMenuGroup,
    SearchMenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Catalog from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Catalog.svelte";
  import DataBase from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/DataBase.svelte";
  import Launch from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Launch.svelte";

  let value = "data";

  const resources = [
    {
      id: "res-pg-test",
      name: "Databases for PostgreSQL-Test",
      icon: DataBase,
    },
  ];
  const catalog = [
    { id: "cat-att-iot", name: "AT&T IoT Data Plans", icon: Catalog },
    { id: "cat-memcache", name: "Data Store for Memcache", icon: DataBase },
    {
      id: "cat-hazardhub",
      name: "HazardHub Property Risk Data API",
      icon: Catalog,
    },
    {
      id: "cat-financial",
      name: "Managed Financial Data API",
      icon: Catalog,
    },
  ];
</script>

<SearchMenu bind:value labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  <SearchMenuGroup label="Resource results">
    <Link slot="action" href="/resources">View all</Link>
    {#each resources as item (item.id)}
      <SearchMenuItem
        text={item.name}
        value={item.id}
        icon={item.icon}
        href="#resource"
      />
    {/each}
  </SearchMenuGroup>

  <SearchMenuGroup label="Catalog results">
    <Link slot="action" href="/catalog">View all</Link>
    {#each catalog as item (item.id)}
      <SearchMenuItem
        text={item.name}
        value={item.id}
        icon={item.icon}
        href="#catalog"
      />
    {/each}
  </SearchMenuGroup>

  <SearchMenuGroup divider>
    <SearchMenuItem
      persistent
      iconRight={Launch}
      href="#support"
      text={`Search "${value}" in Support cases`}
    />
    <SearchMenuItem
      persistent
      iconRight={Launch}
      href="#docs"
      text={`Search "${value}" in Docs`}
    />
  </SearchMenuGroup>
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Recent searches

Set `filter` to `false` on a group to show its items regardless of the search value, for example a list of recent searches. Use the `action` slot to add a header action such as "Clear recent searches".

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Link,
    SearchMenu,
    SearchMenuGroup,
    SearchMenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Time from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Time.svelte";

  let value = "";
  let searchRef = null;

  let recent = [
    { id: "recent-vsi", query: "virtual servers" },
    { id: "recent-starter", query: "mobile starter kits" },
    { id: "recent-vpc", query: "vpc" },
    { id: "recent-schematics", query: "schematics workspace" },
  ];
</script>

<SearchMenu
  bind:value
  bind:ref={searchRef}
  labelText="Search"
  placeholder="Search..."
>
  <SearchMenuGroup label="Recent searches" filter={false}>
    <Link
      slot="action"
      href="#"
      on:click={(e) => {
        e.preventDefault();
        recent = [];
        searchRef?.focus();
      }}
    >
      Clear recent searches
    </Link>
    {#each recent as item (item.id)}
      <SearchMenuItem text={item.query} value={item.id} icon={Time} />
    {/each}
  </SearchMenuGroup>
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Item filter override

Set `filter` on a `SearchMenuItem` to override the group's `filter` (or the menu's `shouldFilter`) for that one item, for example to pin a suggestion inside an otherwise-filtered group.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SearchMenu,
    SearchMenuGroup,
    SearchMenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu labelText="Search" placeholder="Search..." value="test">
  <SearchMenuGroup label="Results">
    <SearchMenuItem text="Databases for TestSQL" />
    <SearchMenuItem text="Data Store for Memcache" />
    <SearchMenuItem text="Pinned: Getting started guide" filter={false} />
  </SearchMenuGroup>
</SearchMenu>
```

### Layout

#### Leading dropdown

Use the `before` slot to render content to the left of the input within a joined bar, for example a [Dropdown](/components/Dropdown) that scopes the search. Bind to the dropdown selection to update the placeholder and filter results. Compose a [Stack](/components/Stack) with a 1px separator between the dropdown and the search input. The results menu matches the search input width, and opening the dropdown closes the search menu.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Box,
    Dropdown,
    SearchMenu,
    SearchMenuItem,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
  let scopeId = "all";

  const scopeItems = [
    { id: "all", text: "All" },
    { id: "networks", text: "Networks" },
    { id: "devices", text: "Devices" },
  ];

  const scopeConfig = {
    all: {
      placeholder: "Search networks and devices",
      types: ["network", "device"],
    },
    networks: {
      placeholder: "Search private networks",
      types: ["network"],
    },
    devices: {
      placeholder: "Search edge gateways",
      types: ["device"],
    },
  };

  const resources = [
    { id: "gw-01", name: "Edge gateway 01", type: "device" },
    { id: "gw-02", name: "Edge gateway 02", type: "device" },
    { id: "gw-lab", name: "Edge gateway lab", type: "device" },
    { id: "net-us-south", name: "Private network us-south", type: "network" },
    { id: "net-eu-de", name: "Private network eu-de", type: "network" },
    { id: "net-ap-tokyo", name: "Private network ap-tokyo", type: "network" },
  ];

  $: config = scopeConfig[scopeId] ?? scopeConfig.all;
  $: placeholder = config.placeholder;
  $: results = resources.filter((item) => config.types.includes(item.type));
</script>

<SearchMenu bind:value {placeholder} labelText="Search">
  <Stack slot="before" orientation="horizontal" align="stretch" gap={0}>
    <Dropdown
      hideLabel
      size="xl"
      titleText="Scope"
      style="width: 12rem"
      bind:selectedId={scopeId}
      items={scopeItems}
      on:select={() => (value = "")}
    />
    <Box aria-hidden="true" width={1} fill="layer-03" />
  </Stack>

  {#each results as item (item.id)}
    <SearchMenuItem text={item.name} value={item.id} />
  {/each}
</SearchMenu>
```

### Menu positioning

Control where and how the results menu renders relative to the input.

#### Top direction

Set `direction` to `"top"` to open the results menu above the input. Useful when space below is limited.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu direction="top" labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  <SearchMenuItem text="Databases for TestSQL" />
  <SearchMenuItem text="Data Store for Memcache" />
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Portal menu

By default, the results menu renders in a floating portal so it can escape parent containers with `overflow: hidden` or z-index stacking contexts. Set it to `false` for the menu to render within the parent container.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu portal={false} labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  <SearchMenuItem text="Databases for TestSQL" />
  <SearchMenuItem text="Data Store for Memcache" />
</SearchMenu>
```

### Matching

As the user types, each `SearchMenuItem` is matched against the search value to decide whether it is shown and which characters of its `text` are highlighted. The `match` prop controls this. It receives the item `text` and the current search value and returns `{ matched, indices }`: `matched` filters the item out when `false`, and `indices` are the character positions highlighted in the text. The default is fuzzy matching.

#### Built-in fuzzy matching

Fuzzy matching prefers a contiguous substring, ranking a prefix above a word boundary above a mid-word occurrence, and falls back to a subsequence match so that "dsm" matches "**D**ata **S**tore for **M**emcache". Matching is case-insensitive. No configuration is required.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu labelText="Search" placeholder="Search..." value="dsm">
  <SearchMenuItem text="Databases for TestSQL" />
  <SearchMenuItem text="Data Store for Memcache" />
  <SearchMenuItem text="AT&T IoT Data Plans" />
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Custom fuzzy options

Import `fuzzyMatch` from `carbon-components-svelte` to reuse the built-in matcher with custom options. Pass an options object as the third argument to tune sensitivity: set `threshold` to a value between `0` and `1` to require a minimum match quality (`0`, the default, accepts any match; `0.5` requires a contiguous substring; `0.7` a word-boundary substring; and `0.9` a prefix). Set `caseSensitive` to `true` to match the exact case. Pass it to the `match` prop.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    fuzzyMatch,
    SearchMenu,
    SearchMenuItem,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "Data";

  const resources = [
    "Data Table",
    "Data Store for Memcache",
    "Databases for TestSQL",
    "AT&T IoT Data Plans",
  ];

  // Reuse the built-in matcher, but raise the sensitivity threshold. A
  // `threshold` of 0.5 requires a contiguous substring, so a scattered
  // subsequence like "dt" (which the default fuzzy matching accepts for
  // "Data Table") no longer matches.
  const match = (text, query) => fuzzyMatch(text, query, { threshold: 0.5 });
</script>

<SearchMenu bind:value {match} labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  {#each resources as text (text)}
    <SearchMenuItem {text} />
  {/each}
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Custom filtering

Provide your own `match` function for full control over the matching logic. The example below matches items by a case-insensitive prefix. Return `matched: false` to filter an item out. Pass a no-op such as `match={() => ({ matched: true })}` to keep every item and disable highlighting entirely.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "data";

  const resources = [
    "Databases for TestSQL",
    "AT&T IoT Data Plans",
    "Data Store for Memcache",
    "HazardHub Property Risk Data API",
    "Managed Financial Data API",
  ];

  // Custom prefix matcher: only items whose text starts with the query match.
  // `matched` filters items out; `indices` are the characters to highlight.
  function match(text, query) {
    const q = query.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (q === "") return { matched: true, indices: [] };
    const matched = text.toLowerCase().startsWith(q);
    return {
      matched,
      indices: matched ? Array.from({ length: q.length }, (_, i) => i) : [],
    };
  }
</script>

<SearchMenu bind:value {match} labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  {#each resources as text (text)}
    <SearchMenuItem {text} />
  {/each}
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Custom filtering with character highlighting

To customize how matched characters render, use the default slot with `let:segments`. Each segment is `{ text, match }`, computed from your `match` function's `indices`, so you can wrap matched runs in your own markup -- no `{@html}` required. The example below applies a yellow highlight. Keep the `{#each}` compact so adjacent segments are not split by whitespace.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "data";

  const resources = [
    "Databases for TestSQL",
    "AT&T IoT Data Plans",
    "Data Store for Memcache",
    "HazardHub Property Risk Data API",
    "Managed Financial Data API",
  ];

  // Custom matcher: a case-insensitive substring match.
  function match(text, query) {
    const q = query.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (q === "") return { matched: true, indices: [] };
    const start = text.toLowerCase().indexOf(q);
    if (start === -1) return { matched: false, indices: [] };
    return {
      matched: true,
      indices: Array.from({ length: q.length }, (_, i) => start + i),
    };
  }
</script>

<!--
  Use the default slot with `let:segments` to render the label yourself. Each
  segment is `{ text, match }`, so no `{@html}` is needed -- wrap matched runs
  in your own markup. Keep the `{#each}` compact so adjacent segments are not
  split by whitespace.
-->
<SearchMenu bind:value {match} labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  {#each resources as text (text)}
    <SearchMenuItem {text} let:segments
      >{#each segments as segment}
        {#if segment.match}
          <mark>{segment.text}</mark>
        {:else}
          {segment.text}
        {/if}
      {/each}</SearchMenuItem
    >
  {/each}
</SearchMenu>

<style>
  mark {
    background: #f1c21b;
    color: #161616;
  }
</style>
```

### Filtering

The `shouldFilter` prop toggles client-side filtering. Client-side matching (the default) and server-side filtering can each be used on their own or combined. Unmatched items stay mounted and are hidden, so later keystrokes only punch visibility and update highlight marks.

#### Server-side results

Set `shouldFilter` to `false` to render results exactly as provided, for example results already filtered by a server. The default matcher still highlights the query within each result; pass a no-op `match={() => ({ matched: true })}` to disable client-side highlighting entirely.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu shouldFilter={false} labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  <SearchMenuItem text="Result rendered as-is" />
  <SearchMenuItem text="Another server result" />
</SearchMenu>
```

#### No results

Provide a `noResults` slot to render an empty state when the search value matches no items.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu labelText="Search" placeholder="Search..." value="no match">
  <SearchMenuItem text="Databases for TestSQL" />
  <SearchMenuItem text="Data Store for Memcache" />
  <svelte:fragment slot="noResults">No results found</svelte:fragment>
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Async results

Combine an async data source with client-side highlighting. Bind to `value`, fetch on input (debounced here), and render the returned items. Because filtering happens on the server (`shouldFilter={false}`), the menu shows exactly what the server returns while the client-side matcher still highlights the query. Set `loading` to render a skeleton menu while fetching (customize the rows with `skeletonCount` or the `loading` slot), and use the `noResults` slot for the empty state.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let value = "";
  let results = [];
  let loading = false;
  let timeout;

  const database = [
    "Databases for PostgreSQL",
    "Databases for MongoDB",
    "Databases for Redis",
    "Db2 on Cloud",
    "Data Store for Memcache",
    "Cloud Object Storage",
    "Watson Machine Learning",
    "Key Protect",
  ];

  // Simulate a server endpoint. The boolean predicate is the server-side match
  // decision -- swap the body for a real `fetch()`.
  function fetchResults(query) {
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      setTimeout(() => {
        const q = query.toLowerCase();
        resolve(database.filter((record) => record.toLowerCase().includes(q)));
      }, 600);
    });
  }

  // Debounce input, then fetch. `shouldFilter={false}` defers filtering to the
  // server; the client still highlights the query within each returned result.
  $: queryResults(value);

  function queryResults(query) {
    clearTimeout(timeout);
    const trimmed = query.trim();
    if (trimmed === "") {
      results = [];
      loading = false;
      return;
    }
    loading = true;
    timeout = setTimeout(async () => {
      results = await fetchResults(trimmed);
      loading = false;
    }, 300);
  }
</script>

<SearchMenu
  bind:value
  {loading}
  shouldFilter={false}
  labelText="Search"
  placeholder="Search..."
>
  {#each results as result (result)}
    <SearchMenuItem text={result} />
  {/each}
  <svelte:fragment slot="noResults">No results for "{value}"</svelte:fragment>
</SearchMenu>
```

### Events

The `select` event fires when an item is activated, carrying the `value`, the `item`, and the originating `event`. The `submit` event fires when pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> without an active item, carrying the current `value`. The `close` event fires when the menu closes, with a `trigger` of `"escape-key"`, `"outside-click"`, `"select"`, or `"blur"`.

#### Result links

Set `href` on a `SearchMenuItem` to render it as a link. Selecting the item with the mouse or <kbd>Enter</kbd> follows the link.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import ArrowRight from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/ArrowRight.svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu labelText="Search" placeholder="Search...">
  <SearchMenuItem
    text="Carbon Design System"
    href="https://carbondesignsystem.com"
    iconRight={ArrowRight}
  />
  <SearchMenuItem
    text="Carbon Components Svelte"
    href="https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-components-svelte"
    iconRight={ArrowRight}
  />
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Free-text submit

```svelte
<script>
  import { SearchMenu, SearchMenuItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SearchMenu
  labelText="Search"
  placeholder="Search..."
  on:submit={(e) => console.log("submit", e.detail.value)}
  on:select={(e) => console.log("select", e.detail)}
>
  <SearchMenuItem text="Databases for TestSQL" />
  <SearchMenuItem text="Data Store for Memcache" />
</SearchMenu>
```

#### Search input and menu

Grey out both the input and the menu by composing [Search](/components/Search) with the `skeleton` prop and `SearchMenuSkeleton` for the results menu. Place `SearchMenuSkeleton` inside a `bx--search-menu__search` wrapper so the menu aligns with the input. For a loading state on an interactive menu, prefer the `loading` prop shown in [Async results](#async-results).


### Component API

#### `SearchMenu` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `T` | Specify the value of the search input. | `""` |
| `open` (Reactive) | `boolean` | Whether the results menu is visible. Driven by focus and available content. | `false` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLInputElement` | Obtain a reference to the input HTML element. | `null` |
| `menuRef` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLDivElement` | Obtain a reference to the menu HTML element. | `null` |
| `shouldFilter` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to filter items by the search value using fuzzy matching.<br />Unmatched items stay mounted and are hidden so later keystrokes do not<br />recreate option nodes. | `true` |
| `match` | `(text: string, query: string) => { matched: boolean; indices?: number[] }` | Override how the search value is matched against each item's `text`.<br />Receives the item `text` and the current search value, and returns whether<br />the item `matched` along with the `indices` of characters to highlight.<br />Defaults to fuzzy matching. Supply your own function for custom filtering<br />and highlighting, or pass a no-op like `() => ({ matched: true })` to keep<br />every item and disable highlighting. | `fuzzyMatch` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | Specify the size of the search input. | `"xl"` |
| `menuSize` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | Specify the size of the results menu, independent of the input `size`.<br />Defaults to the input `size`. | _undefined_ |
| `light` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable the light variant | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the search input | `false` |
| `loading` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render a skeleton menu while results are loading, for<br />example while fetching server-side results. Override the placeholder rows<br />with the `loading` slot. | `false` |
| `skeletonCount` | `number` | Specify the number of skeleton rows rendered while `loading` | `4` |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Specify the placeholder text | `"Search..."` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
| `closeButtonLabelText` | `string` | Specify the close button label text | `"Clear search input"` |
| `icon` | `any` | Specify the icon to render. | _undefined_ |
| `direction` | `"bottom" \| "top"` | Specify the direction of the results menu. | `"bottom"` |
| `portal` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to render the menu in a portal to escape `overflow: hidden` containers | `true` |
| `searchClass` | `string` | Specify a class passed to the inner Search element | `""` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the search input | `uniqueId()` |

## Select

### Basic

Create a basic select menu with select item components. The first item's value is used as the default if selected is not set.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Select, SelectItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select
  labelText="Carbon theme"
  on:change={(e) => console.log("value", e.target.value)}
>
  <SelectItem value="white" />
  <SelectItem value="g10" />
  <SelectItem value="g80" />
  <SelectItem value="g90" />
  <SelectItem value="g100" />
</Select>
```

### Reactive

Bind to `selected` for reactive updates, or listen for the `update` event directly--Select dispatches it whenever the selected value changes, which is what powers the two-way binding.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Select, SelectItem, Stack } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selected = "g10";
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <Select
    labelText="Carbon theme"
    helperText="Selected: {selected}"
    bind:selected
  >
    <SelectItem value="white" text="White" />
    <SelectItem value="g10" text="Gray 10" />
    <SelectItem value="g80" text="Gray 80" />
    <SelectItem value="g90" text="Gray 90" />
    <SelectItem value="g100" text="Gray 100" />
  </Select>
  <Button
    kind="tertiary"
    size="small"
    disabled={selected === "g90"}
    on:click={() => (selected = "g90")}
  >
    Set to "g90"
  </Button>
</Stack>
```

### Content

Customize the option text, the initial selection, the label, and how options are grouped.

#### Custom item text

Customize each option's display text with the `text` prop on SelectItem.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Select, SelectItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select
  labelText="Carbon theme"
  on:change={(e) => console.log("value", e.target.value)}
>
  <SelectItem value="white" text="White" />
  <SelectItem value="g10" text="Gray 10" />
  <SelectItem value="g80" text="Gray 80" />
  <SelectItem value="g90" text="Gray 90" />
  <SelectItem value="g100" text="Gray 100" />
</Select>
```

#### Initial selection

```svelte
<script>
  import { Select, SelectItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select
  labelText="Carbon theme"
  selected="g10"
  on:change={(e) => console.log("value", e.target.value)}
>
  <SelectItem value="white" text="White" />
  <SelectItem value="g10" text="Gray 10" />
  <SelectItem value="g80" text="Gray 80" />
  <SelectItem value="g90" text="Gray 90" />
  <SelectItem value="g100" text="Gray 100" />
</Select>
```

#### Helper text

Add descriptive text below the select menu.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Select, SelectItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select
  helperText="Carbon offers 4 themes (2 light, 3 dark)"
  labelText="Carbon theme"
  selected="g10"
>
  <SelectItem value="white" text="White" />
  <SelectItem value="g10" text="Gray 10" />
  <SelectItem value="g80" text="Gray 80" />
  <SelectItem value="g90" text="Gray 90" />
  <SelectItem value="g100" text="Gray 100" />
</Select>
```

#### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Select, SelectItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select hideLabel labelText="Carbon theme" selected="g10">
  <SelectItem value="white" text="White" />
  <SelectItem value="g10" text="Gray 10" />
  <SelectItem value="g80" text="Gray 80" />
  <SelectItem value="g90" text="Gray 90" />
  <SelectItem value="g100" text="Gray 100" />
</Select>
```

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to provide custom label content.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Select, SelectItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select labelText="">
  <strong slot="labelChildren">Carbon theme</strong>
  <SelectItem value="white" text="White" />
  <SelectItem value="g10" text="Gray 10" />
  <SelectItem value="g80" text="Gray 80" />
  <SelectItem value="g90" text="Gray 90" />
  <SelectItem value="g100" text="Gray 100" />
</Select>
```

#### Remove label

Set `noLabel` to `true` to omit the label element entirely. Unlike `hideLabel`, which keeps the label available to screen readers, `noLabel` removes it from the DOM. Provide an accessible name some other way, such as `aria-label` (forwarded through to the select element), when using `noLabel`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Select, SelectItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select
  noLabel
  labelText="Carbon theme"
  selected="g10"
  aria-label="Carbon theme"
>
  <SelectItem value="white" text="White" />
  <SelectItem value="g10" text="Gray 10" />
  <SelectItem value="g80" text="Gray 80" />
  <SelectItem value="g90" text="Gray 90" />
  <SelectItem value="g100" text="Gray 100" />
</Select>
```

#### Item groups

Group related options using select item group components. The example below also combines `disabled` and `hidden` on the first `SelectItem` to create a non-selectable placeholder that appears as the initial value but is absent from the open option list.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    SelectItemGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select labelText="Carbon theme" selected="0">
  <SelectItem value="0" text="Select a theme" disabled hidden />
  <SelectItemGroup label="Light theme">
    <SelectItem value="white" text="White" />
    <SelectItem value="g10" text="Gray 10" />
  </SelectItemGroup>
  <SelectItemGroup label="Dark theme">
    <SelectItem value="g80" text="Gray 80" />
    <SelectItem value="g90" text="Gray 90" />
    <SelectItem value="g100" text="Gray 100" />
  </SelectItemGroup>
</Select>
```

#### Disabled group

Set `disabled` on `SelectItemGroup` to disable every item within a group.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Select,
    SelectItem,
    SelectItemGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select labelText="Carbon theme" selected="white">
  <SelectItemGroup label="Light theme">
    <SelectItem value="white" text="White" />
    <SelectItem value="g10" text="Gray 10" />
  </SelectItemGroup>
  <SelectItemGroup label="Dark theme" disabled>
    <SelectItem value="g80" text="Gray 80" />
    <SelectItem value="g90" text="Gray 90" />
    <SelectItem value="g100" text="Gray 100" />
  </SelectItemGroup>
</Select>
```

### Fluid

Set `fluid` to embed the label inside the field. Fluid selects work standalone or inside [FluidForm](/components/FluidForm), which applies the variant automatically. The fluid variant cannot be combined with the inline variant.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Select, SelectItem } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Select fluid labelText="Carbon theme" selected="g10">
  <SelectItem value="white" text="White" />
  <SelectItem value="g10" text="Gray 10" />
  <SelectItem value="g80" text="Gray 80" />
  <SelectItem value="g90" text="Gray 90" />
  <SelectItem value="g100" text="Gray 100" />
</Select>
```

#### Custom label

Use the `labelChildren` slot to render custom label content, such as a tooltip icon.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Select, SelectItem, TooltipIcon } from "carbon-components-svelte";
  import Information from "carbon-icons-svelte/lib/Information.svelte";
</script>

<Select fluid labelText="Carbon theme" selected="g10">
  <svelte:fragment slot="labelChildren">
    Carbon theme
    <TooltipIcon
      tooltipText="Themes determine the color palette of the page."
      icon={Information}
    />
  </svelte:fragment>
  <SelectItem value="white" text="White" />
  <SelectItem value="g10" text="Gray 10" />
  <SelectItem value="g80" text="Gray 80" />
  <SelectItem value="g90" text="Gray 90" />
  <SelectItem value="g100" text="Gray 100" />
</Select>
```

### Component API

#### `Select` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selected` (Reactive) | `Value \| undefined` | Specify the selected item value. | _undefined_ |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLSelectElement` | Obtain a reference to the select HTML element. | `null` |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "xl"` | Set the size of the select input. | _undefined_ |
| `inline` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the inline variant | `false` |
| `light` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable the light variant | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the select element | `false` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the select element | `uniqueId()` |
| `name` | `string` | Specify a name attribute for the select element. | _undefined_ |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate an invalid state | `false` |
| `invalidText` | `string` | Specify the invalid state text | `""` |
| `warn` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate a warning state | `false` |
| `warnText` | `string` | Specify the warning state text | `""` |
| `helperText` | `string` | Specify the helper text | `""` |
| `noLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to not render a label | `false` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text | `false` |
| `required` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to mark the field as required | `false` |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for the select to be read-only | `false` |
| `fluid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the fluid variant.<br />Inherited from the parent `FluidForm` context,<br />so it does not need to be set when used inside `FluidForm`.<br />Cannot be combined with the inline variant. | `false` |

| --------------- | ----------------------- |
| `default`       | `Record<string, never>` |
| `labelChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |

| `on:change` |
| `on:focus`  |
| `on:input`  |

| `hidden` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to hide the option | `false` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the option | `false` |
| `class` | `string` | Specify the class of the `option` element. | _undefined_ |
| `style` | `string` | Specify the style of the `option` element. | _undefined_ |

## SelectableTile

### Basic

Group multiple selectable tiles together for multi-selection scenarios.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SelectableTileGroup
  legendText="Select options"
  name="options"
  selected={["option1", "option2"]}
>
  <SelectableTile value="option1">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="option2">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="option3">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
</SelectableTileGroup>
```

### Reactive

#### One-way binding

Update selected values using the `select` and `deselect` events.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const values = ["Lite plan", "Standard plan", "Plus plan"];

  let selected = [values[0], values[1]];
</script>

<SelectableTileGroup
  legendText="Service pricing tiers"
  name="plan"
  on:select={({ detail }) => (selected = [...selected, detail])}
  on:deselect={({ detail }) =>
    (selected = selected.filter((v) => v !== detail))}
>
  {#each values as value}
    <SelectableTile {value} selected={selected.includes(value)}>
      {value}
    </SelectableTile>
  {/each}
</SelectableTileGroup>

<br />
Selected: <strong>{selected.join(", ") || "None"}</strong>
```

#### Two-way binding

Bind to `selected` for simpler state management.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  const values = ["Lite plan", "Standard plan", "Plus plan"];

  let selected = [values[0], values[1]];
</script>

<Stack gap={5}>
  <SelectableTileGroup
    legendText="Service pricing tiers"
    name="plan"
    bind:selected
  >
    {#each values as value}
      <SelectableTile {value}>{value}</SelectableTile>
    {/each}
  </SelectableTileGroup>
  <div>Selected: <strong>{selected.join(", ") || "None"}</strong></div>
  <Button
    size="small"
    disabled={selected.length === 1 && selected[0] === values[1]}
    on:click={() => (selected = [values[1]])}
  >
    Set to "{values[1]}" only
  </Button>
</Stack>
```

### Legend

#### Custom content

Use the `legendChildren` slot on `SelectableTileGroup` to provide custom legend content instead of `legendText`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SelectableTileGroup
  name="options-legend-slot"
  selected={["option1", "option2"]}
>
  <strong slot="legendChildren">Select options</strong>
  <SelectableTile value="option1">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="option2">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="option3">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
</SelectableTileGroup>
```

#### Hidden

Hide the legend visually by setting `hideLegend` to `true`. The legend remains available to screen readers.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SelectableTileGroup
  hideLegend
  legendText="Select options"
  name="options-hidden-legend"
  selected={["option1"]}
>
  <SelectableTile value="option1">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="option2">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="option3">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
</SelectableTileGroup>
```

### Light

Use the light variant for light backgrounds.

```svelte
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
```

### Disabled

Disable specific tiles, or the entire group, to prevent selection.

#### Individual tiles

Disable specific tiles to prevent interaction.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SelectableTileGroup
  legendText="Select options"
  name="options-disabled"
  selected={["option1"]}
>
  <SelectableTile value="option1">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile disabled value="option2">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile disabled value="option3">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
</SelectableTileGroup>
```

#### Entire group

Disable every tile at once by setting `disabled` on `SelectableTileGroup`. This prevents selection natively through the underlying `fieldset`, but doesn't apply the muted disabled tile styling shown above--set `disabled` on each `SelectableTile` too for the visual state.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SelectableTileGroup
  legendText="Select options"
  name="options-disabled-group"
  selected={["option1", "option2"]}
  disabled
>
  <SelectableTile value="option1">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="option2">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="option3">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
</SelectableTileGroup>
```

### Checkmark label

Customize the ARIA label announced for a tile's checkmark icon with `iconDescription`. Defaults to `"Tile checkmark"`.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    SelectableTile,
    SelectableTileGroup,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SelectableTileGroup
  legendText="Select options"
  name="options-checkmark-label"
  selected={["option1"]}
>
  <SelectableTile iconDescription="Option 1 selected" value="option1">
    Multi-select Tile
  </SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="option2">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
  <SelectableTile value="option3">Multi-select Tile</SelectableTile>
</SelectableTileGroup>
```

### Component API

#### `SelectableTileGroup` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selected` (Reactive) | `T[]` | Specify the selected tile values. | `[]` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the tile group | `false` |
| `name` | `string \| undefined` | Specify a name attribute for the checkbox inputs. | _undefined_ |
| `legendText` | `string` | Specify the legend text.<br />Alternatively, use the named slot "legendChildren". | `""` |
| `hideLegend` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the legend | `false` |

#### `SelectableTileGroup` slots

| Slot             | Detail                  |
| ---------------- | ----------------------- |
| `default`        | `Record<string, never>` |
| `legendChildren` | `Record<string, never>` |

#### `SelectableTileGroup` dispatched events

| Event         | Detail |
| ------------- | ------ |
| `on:deselect` | `T`    |
| `on:select`   | `T`    |

## SessionStorage

### Basic

See how the component maintains state within a session. Toggle the switch and refresh the page to see the persisted state. State is cleared when the tab is closed. Unlike [LocalStorage](/components/LocalStorage), data is isolated per tab.

The component listens for the [storage event](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/storage_event) so updates from another same-origin document in the same tab (for example, an iframe) stay in sync. Session storage is isolated per tab, so this event does not propagate across tabs or windows. When the key is removed from a shared session context, the bound value resets to undefined so the next local write does not re-persist stale data.

This example logs the `save` and `update` events as they fire -- see [Events](#events) for what each one means and its payload shape.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SessionStorage, Toggle } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let toggled = false;
  let events = [];

  $: document.documentElement.setAttribute("theme", toggled ? "g100" : "white");
</script>

<SessionStorage
  key="dark-mode-session"
  bind:value={toggled}
  on:save={() => {
    events = [...events, { event: "on:save" }];
  }}
  on:update={({ detail }) => {
    events = [...events, { event: "on:update", detail }];
  }}
/>

<Toggle size="sm" labelText="Dark mode" bind:toggled />

<br />

<pre>{JSON.stringify(events, null, 2)}</pre>
```

### Persisting objects and arrays

The bound value can be any JSON-serializable data; objects and arrays are serialized with JSON.stringify. The component compares the serialized form to decide when to write, which has two consequences:

- Reassigning to a new object or array with **identical contents** does not trigger a redundant write.
- **In-place mutations** (for example, changing a nested theme property) persist only when you signal the change to Svelte. Reassign the value (`value = { ...value, theme: "light" }`) or use the self-assignment idiom (`value = value`); a bare mutation alone will not re-render and therefore will not persist.

In this example, the text inputs bind directly to nested properties and the button mutates the object in place. Edit a field and refresh the page to confirm the change is persisted within the session.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    SessionStorage,
    Stack,
    TextInput,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  // A nested object value. Editing a nested field -- either through a two-way
  // binding or an explicit in-place mutation signalled with `value = value` --
  // is persisted because the component compares the serialized form.
  let settings = { profile: { name: "Ada", role: "Engineer" }, visits: 0 };
  let events = [];
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <SessionStorage
    key="session-storage-object-example"
    bind:value={settings}
    on:update={({ detail }) => {
      events = [...events, { event: "on:update", detail }];
    }}
  />

  <div>
    Edit the nested fields below, then refresh the page to confirm the changes
    survive within the session. The two-way bindings mutate
    <code>settings</code>
    in place; the component still persists them.
  </div>

  <TextInput
    labelText="Name (binds to settings.profile.name)"
    bind:value={settings.profile.name}
  />

  <TextInput
    labelText="Role (binds to settings.profile.role)"
    bind:value={settings.profile.role}
  />

  <Button
    size="small"
    on:click={() => {
      settings.visits += 1; // in-place mutation
      settings = settings; // signal the change to Svelte
    }}
  >
    Increment visits ({settings.visits})
  </Button>

  <div>
    <strong>Current value:</strong>
    <pre>{JSON.stringify(settings, null, 2)}</pre>
  </div>

  <div>
    <strong>Updates (note prevValue is a true snapshot):</strong>
    <pre>{JSON.stringify(events, null, 2)}</pre>
  </div>
</Stack>
```

### Reactive key

The storage key is also reactive -- set `key` to switch between contexts, useful for per-user settings.

In this example, each user has their own theme preference stored under a separate key. When you switch users, the component automatically loads that user's saved preference.

Switching keys only hydrates the bound value from storage; it does not dispatch [`update`](#update). The event log below should stay empty when you change users and only record entries when you change the theme.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    RadioButton,
    RadioButtonGroup,
    SessionStorage,
    Stack,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let selectedUser = "user-1";
  let theme = "white";
  let events = [];

  $: storageKey = `session-storage-reactive-example-${selectedUser}`;
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <div>
    Try selecting different users and changing their theme preferences. Each
    user's preference is stored separately and persists within the session.
  </div>
  <SessionStorage
    key={storageKey}
    bind:value={theme}
    on:update={({ detail }) => {
      events = [...events, { event: "on:update", detail }];
    }}
  />
  <RadioButtonGroup legendText="Select user" bind:selected={selectedUser}>
    <RadioButton labelText="User 1" value="user-1" />
    <RadioButton labelText="User 2" value="user-2" />
    <RadioButton labelText="User 3" value="user-3" />
  </RadioButtonGroup>
  <RadioButtonGroup legendText="Theme preference" bind:selected={theme}>
    <RadioButton labelText="White" value="white" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Gray 10" value="g10" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Gray 80" value="g80" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Gray 90" value="g90" />
    <RadioButton labelText="Gray 100" value="g100" />
  </RadioButtonGroup>
  <Stack gap={2}>
    <div>
      <strong>Current key:</strong>
      {storageKey}
    </div>
    <div>
      <strong>Current theme:</strong>
      {theme}
    </div>
  </Stack>
  <strong> Updates: </strong>
  <pre>{JSON.stringify(events, null, 2)}</pre>
</Stack>
```

### Disabling sync

With sync enabled by default, the component listens for storage events and updates the bound value when another same-origin document in this tab writes the same key, such as an iframe. Set `sync="off"` to ignore those writes. The component still loads storage on mount and saves your own changes.

Session storage is already per tab, so this matters mainly when an iframe shares the session. Turn sync off when the host page should not follow iframe writes, or when the app handles conflicts itself. Sync is reactive, so you can change it at runtime.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SessionStorage } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SessionStorage key="draft" bind:value sync="off" />
```

### Clear item, clear all

The component provides methods to manage stored data:

| Method      | Description                       |
| ----------- | --------------------------------- |
| `clearItem` | Remove a specific key-value pair. |
| `clearAll`  | Remove all stored data.           |

Use `bind:this` to access these methods. They only clear browser storage in the current tab; they do not reset the bound value. To clear both storage and the bound value, reset the value yourself after calling clearItem or clearAll.

In this example, toggle the switch and refresh the page to confirm the value persists, then try either button to clear storage.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    Button,
    SessionStorage,
    Stack,
    Toggle,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";

  let storage;
  let toggled = false;

  $: document.documentElement.setAttribute("theme", toggled ? "g100" : "white");
</script>

<Stack gap={6}>
  <SessionStorage bind:this={storage} bind:value={toggled} />

  <Toggle size="sm" labelText="Dark mode" bind:toggled />

  <div>
    Toggle the switch, then refresh the page to confirm the value persists.
    <code>clearItem</code>
    removes just this key; <code>clearAll</code> removes every key in session storage.
    Either way, the toggle itself is left untouched until you refresh.
  </div>

  <Stack gap={3} orientation="horizontal">
    <Button size="small" on:click={() => storage.clearItem()}>
      Clear item
    </Button>
    <Button size="small" kind="danger" on:click={() => storage.clearAll()}>
      Clear all
    </Button>
  </Stack>
</Stack>
```

### Events

Respond to storage writes, cross-document updates, and write failures.

#### Save

Dispatched once on mount, when `key` is not already present in storage -- right after the component seeds storage with the current `value`. The payload is always `null`.

This fires the first time a key is used in the current session, and again after storage is cleared and the page is refreshed (see [Clear item, clear all](#clear-item-clear-all)). The [Basic](#basic) example above logs this event.

#### Update

Dispatched whenever the stored value changes: after a local bound-value write, or after `sync` picks up a matching write from another same-origin document in this tab (see [Disabling sync](#disabling-sync)). The payload is `{ prevValue, value }`; `prevValue` is a snapshot taken before the change, not a live reference to the current value.

Switching `key` hydrates the bound value from storage but does not dispatch this event (see [Reactive key](#reactive-key)).

The [Basic](#basic), [Persisting objects and arrays](#persisting-objects-and-arrays), and [Reactive key](#reactive-key) examples above all log this event.

#### Error

Dispatched when a write to session storage fails -- for example, when storage quota is exceeded, or access is denied such as in a private browsing mode that blocks Web Storage. The payload is `{ error }`, where `error` is the value thrown by the underlying `sessionStorage.setItem` call.

```svelte
<script>
  import { SessionStorage } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<SessionStorage
  key="draft"
  bind:value
  on:error={({ detail }) => console.error("Failed to persist:", detail.error)}
/>
```

---

### Component API

#### `SessionStorage` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `T` | Provide a value to persist. | `""` |
| `key` | `string` | Specify the session storage key. | `"session-storage-key"` |
| `sync` | `"on" \| "off"` | `"off"` ignores storage events from other documents in this tab (e.g. an<br />iframe). `"on"` (default) keeps the previous behavior. | `"on"` |
| `clearItem` | `() => void` | Remove the persisted key value from the browser's session storage.<br />Note: this only clears storage; the bound `value` is left untouched.<br />If `value` mutates afterwards, it will be re-persisted. Reset `value`<br />yourself if you want it cleared as well. | _undefined_ |
| `clearAll` | `() => void` | Clear all key values from the browser's session storage.<br />Note: this only clears storage; the bound `value` is left untouched.<br />If `value` mutates afterwards, it will be re-persisted. Reset `value`<br />yourself if you want it cleared as well. | _undefined_ |

#### `SessionStorage` dispatched events

| Event | Detail | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on:error` | `{ error: unknown }` | Fires when a write to sessionStorage fails (e.g. quota exceeded or access denied). |
| `on:save` | `null` |  |
| `on:update` | `{<br />  prevValue: T;<br />  value: T;<br />}` | Fires when the stored value changes, either from a bound value update or when sessionStorage is modified by another same origin document in this tab (e.g. an iframe). Set `sync` to `"off"` to ignore those external updates. |

## Slider

### Basic

Create a basic slider with a label and the default range from 0 to 100.

```svelte

</script>

<Slider labelText="Instances" value={0} />
```

### Labels and layout

Control how the slider label, text input, and width render.

```svelte
<Slider labelText="Instances" fullWidth value={0} />
```

#### Hidden label

Hide the label visually by setting `hideLabel` to `true`. The label remains available to screen readers.


#### Custom label

```svelte
  <strong slot="labelChildren">Instances</strong>

```

```svelte

  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider labelText="Instances" hideTextInput value={0} />
```

#### Input type

Set `inputType` to change the native `type` attribute of the text input--for example, `"text"` to avoid the browser's built-in number spinner controls. The bound `value` stays numeric regardless of `inputType`.

```svelte

  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider inputType="text" labelText="Instances" value={0} />
```

### Range and steps

Control the allowed values and increment.

#### Custom range

Set `min`, `max`, `minLabel`, and `maxLabel` to customize the range.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  value={100}
/>
```

#### Custom step

Set `step` to control increment size.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  value={100}
  step={10}
/>
```

#### Step multiplier

Set `stepMultiplier` to control how far Shift + Arrow key presses move the value. Holding Shift while pressing an arrow key moves the value by `(max - min) / stepMultiplier`, rounded to the nearest `step`, instead of a single step. Defaults to `4`.

```svelte
<script>
  import { Slider } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  value={100}
  step={10}
  stepMultiplier={2}
/>
```

### Formatting

Control how range labels and `aria-valuetext` are displayed.

#### Formatted values

Use `formatValue` to format range labels and `aria-valuetext` (for example currency or percent). The text input and bound `value` stay numeric.

```svelte
<script>
  import {
    RangeSlider,
    RangeSliderSkeleton,
    Slider,
    SliderSkeleton,
  } from "carbon-components-svelte";
</script>

<Slider
  labelText="Budget"
  value={50}
  formatValue={(v) =>
    new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", {
      style: "currency",
      currency: "USD",
      maximumFractionDigits: 0,
    }).format(v)}
/>

<Slider labelText="Opacity" value={75} formatValue={(v) => `${v}%`} />

## Marks Set `marks` to show tick marks along the track. Pass an array of stops
with optional labels, or set `marks` to `true` to tick every `step`. Marks are
visual only; snapping still follows `step`.

<Slider
  labelText="Intensity"
  hideTextInput
  min={0}
  max={3}
  step={1}
  value={1}
  marks={[
    { value: 0, label: "Off" },
    { value: 1, label: "Low" },
    { value: 2, label: "Med" },
    { value: 3, label: "High" },
  ]}
/>

### Every step Set `marks` to `true` to place a tick at every `step`.

<Slider
  labelText="Instances"
  hideTextInput
  min={0}
  max={10}
  step={2}
  value={4}
  marks
/>

## Light Use the light variant for light backgrounds.

<Slider
  light
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  value={100}
  step={10}
/>

## Events Respond to value changes as the user drags the handle, uses the
keyboard, or edits the text input. Use `on:input` to listen for every value
while dragging or pressing an arrow key, and `on:change` to listen for committed
changes--when the drag ends, an arrow key is pressed, or the text input is
committed. Both events dispatch the numeric value directly as `event.detail`.

<Slider
  on:input={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // number
  on:change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // number
  labelText="Instances"
  value={0}
/>

## States Communicate validation and interaction states. ### Invalid Set
`invalid` to `true` to show a validation error. Invalid takes precedence over
the [warning state](#warning) when both are set.

<Slider
  invalid
  invalidText="Value must be a multiple of 10"
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  value={105}
  step={10}
/>

### Warning Set `warn` to `true` to show a warning. The warning icon appears
next to the input field, with a message below the slider.

<Slider
  warn
  warnText="Value must be an increment of 5"
  labelText="Slider (must be an increment of 5)"
  min={0}
  max={100}
  value={51}
  step={5}
/>

### Disabled Set `disabled` to `true` to prevent interaction.

<Slider
  disabled
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  value={100}
  step={10}
/>

### Read-only Set `readonly` to `true` to display a value while preventing
changes.

<Slider
  readonly
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  value={100}
  step={10}
/>

## Range slider Use `RangeSlider` to select a range with two handles. Bind to
`value` for the lower bound and `valueUpper` for the upper bound. `RangeSlider`
supports the same layout and state options as `Slider`.

<RangeSlider labelText="Range" value={10} valueUpper={90} />

### Full width Set `fullWidth` to `true` for the range slider to span the full
width of its container.

<RangeSlider labelText="Range" fullWidth value={10} valueUpper={90} />

### Hidden text inputs Set `hideTextInput` to `true` to hide both numeric inputs
while keeping the slider.

<RangeSlider labelText="Range" hideTextInput value={0} valueUpper={100} />

### Custom range and step Set `min`, `max`, and `step` to customize the range.

<RangeSlider
  labelText="Runtime memory (MB)"
  min={10}
  max={990}
  maxLabel="990 MB"
  step={10}
  value={100}
  valueUpper={500}
/>

### Formatted values `formatValue` applies to both thumbs' `aria-valuetext` and
the range labels. Bound `value` / `valueUpper` stay numeric.

<RangeSlider
  labelText="Price range"
  value={20}
  valueUpper={80}
  formatValue={(v) =>
    new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", {
      style: "currency",
      currency: "USD",
      maximumFractionDigits: 0,
    }).format(v)}
/>

### Marks Set `marks` the same way as on `Slider` for tick marks and optional
labels.

<RangeSlider
  labelText="Intensity"
  hideTextInput
  min={0}
  max={3}
  step={1}
  value={0}
  valueUpper={2}
  marks={[
    { value: 0, label: "Off" },
    { value: 1, label: "Low" },
    { value: 2, label: "Med" },
    { value: 3, label: "High" },
  ]}
/>

### Handle labels Set `ariaLabelInput` and `ariaLabelInputUpper` to distinguish
the lower and upper bound handles for screen reader users. Defaults to `"Lower
bound"` and `"Upper bound"`.

<RangeSlider
  ariaLabelInput="Minimum price"
  ariaLabelInputUpper="Maximum price"
  labelText="Price range"
  value={20}
  valueUpper={80}
/>

### Events Use `on:input` and `on:change` the same way as `Slider`. Both events
dispatch `{(value, valueUpper)}` as `event.detail`.

<RangeSlider
  on:input={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // { value: number; valueUpper: number }
  on:change={(e) => console.log(e.detail)}
  // { value: number; valueUpper: number }
  labelText="Range"
  value={10}
  valueUpper={90}
/>

### Invalid Set `invalid` to `true` to show a validation error. Invalid takes
precedence over the [warning state](#warning) when both are set.

<RangeSlider
  invalid
  invalidText="Values must be a multiple of 10"
  labelText="Range"
  min={0}
  max={100}
  step={10}
  value={15}
  valueUpper={85}
/>

### Warning Set `warn` to `true` to show a warning. A warning icon appears next
to each input field, with a message below the slider.

<RangeSlider
  warn
  warnText="Values must be an increment of 5"
  labelText="Range"
  min={0}
  max={100}
  step={5}
  value={11}
  valueUpper={89}
/>

### Disabled Set `disabled` to `true` to prevent interaction.

<RangeSlider disabled labelText="Range" value={10} valueUpper={90} />

### Read-only Set `readonly` to `true` to display values while preventing
changes.

<RangeSlider readonly labelText="Range" value={10} valueUpper={90} />

## Skeleton Show a loading state with the skeleton variant.

<SliderSkeleton />

### Without label Show a loading state without a label.

<SliderSkeleton hideLabel />

### Range slider Show a loading state with the range slider skeleton variant.

<RangeSliderSkeleton />

#### Without label Show a loading state without a label.

<RangeSliderSkeleton hideLabel />
```

#### `Slider` props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (Reactive) | `number` | Specify the value of the slider. | `0` |
| `ref` (Reactive) | `null \| HTMLDivElement` | Obtain a reference to the HTML element. | `null` |
| `max` | `number` | Set the maximum slider value | `100` |
| `maxLabel` | `string` | Specify the label for the max value | `""` |
| `min` | `number` | Set the minimum slider value | `0` |
| `minLabel` | `string` | Specify the label for the min value | `""` |
| `formatValue` | `undefined \| ((value: number) => string)` | Format displayed values for range labels and `aria-valuetext`.<br />Does not change the numeric model; the text input stays numeric. | _undefined_ |
| `step` | `number` | Set the step value | `1` |
| `marks` | `boolean \| ReadonlyArray<{ value: number; label?: string }>` | Show tick marks along the track.<br />Set to `true` to place a tick at every `step`, or pass an array of<br />`{ value, label? }` for specific stops with optional labels below the track.<br />Marks are visual only; snapping still follows `step`. | `false` |
| `stepMultiplier` | `number` | Set the step multiplier value | `4` |
| `required` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to require a value | `false` |
| `inputType` | `string` | Specify the input type | `"number"` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to disable the slider | `false` |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to use the read-only variant | `false` |
| `light` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to enable the light variant | `false` |
| `hideTextInput` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to hide the text input | `false` |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | Set to `true` for the slider to span<br />the full width of its containing element. | `false` |
| `id` | `string` | Set an id for the slider div element | `uniqueId()` |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate an invalid state | `false` |
| `invalidText` | `string` | Specify the invalid state text | `""` |
| `warn` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to indicate a warning state | `false` |
| `warnText` | `string` | Specify the warning state text | `""` |
| `labelText` | `string` | Specify the label text.<br />Alternatively, use the "labelChildren" slot. | `""` |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` | Set to `true` to visually hide the label text | `false` |
| `name` | `string` | Set a name for the slider element | `""` |
